NAO — Digital Transformation of Services

global_cases.case_name: Singapore INTELLLEX Legal AI / SAL Ventures
global_cases.problem_solved: Singapore lawyers and legal aid workers faced the task of manually searching 500,000+ Singapore court decisions plus Commonwealth case law for relevant precedents. Legal research was a significant cost barrier for smaller firms and for the State Courts (community justice). The Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) funded development of AI-assisted legal research tools to democratise access to case law.
global_cases.architecture_summary: INTELLLEX platform: semantic search over Singapore Law Watch case database plus Commonwealth Legal Information Institute data. NLP pipeline: case classification (by area of law), legal proposition extraction, citation network analysis. Judgement summaries auto-generated using extractive + abstractive summarisation. Integration with Singapore Statutes Online. Later expanded to include LawNet (SAL's official legal database). Cloud-hosted (AWS Singapore Region). Annual subscription model for law firms; subsidised access for legal aid bureaus.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 2,000+ active users by 2022. Legal aid research time: 35% reduction. Adoption by Community Legal Clinics (pro bono). Integrated into Singapore Law Watch portal. Partnership with 8 Singapore law schools for academic use. Expanded to HK and Malaysia jurisdictions.
global_cases.failure_modes: Commercial viability challenged by LexisNexis/Thomson Reuters incumbency. High initial pricing limited SME law firm adoption. AI hallucination risk in case summaries — users needed legal training to identify errors. Cross-jurisdiction expansion introduced inconsistent quality (Singapore NLP models underperformed on Malaysian legal documents).
global_cases.replicability_factors: Architecture is replicable for any jurisdiction with a digitised court decision database. SAL has shared methodology at ASEAN legal technology conferences. Singapore's model of government-subsidised legal AI for legal aid is directly applicable to UZ/KG legal aid reform context.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has a digitised court decision database (sud.uz) and the mandate for AI in courts (УП-140). INTELLLEX architecture — semantic search + case summarisation — is the Phase 1 tool that can be built on UZ court decisions corpus. Russian-language NLP capability exists (Yandex, Sber). Key adaptation: Uzbek legal system is Russian-language + Uzbek procedural code. Cost: $1-3M initial tool is affordable. Legal aid application (free access for low-income citizens) is politically valuable.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has court decisions database (cbd.minjust.gov.kg publishes legal acts; court decisions less systematically published). Phase 1 for KG: improve publication completeness of court decisions, then build search tool. Russian-language NLP applies. Legal aid application especially relevant given KG's limited legal aid infrastructure. Cost: $1-2M including corpus digitisation.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian-language legal NLP model fine-tuning on UZ/KG court corpus. Uzbek-language extension for UZ. Kyrgyz-language extension for KG. Institutional hosting within Ministry of Justice or Supreme Court to ensure data sovereignty and sustainability.

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan Anti-Corruption Agency AI Monitoring System
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan's Agency for Financial Monitoring (AFM) and Anti-Corruption Agency (Adildik Alany) needed tools to detect patterns of corruption in public procurement, government asset declarations, and bank transaction flows. Manual review of 500,000+ public procurement transactions/year was impossible at scale. AI-based anomaly detection and network analysis tools were needed to identify suspicious patterns, conflicts of interest, and unexplained wealth.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Three analytical modules: (1) Procurement Anomaly Detector — ML classifier on public procurement data (samruk-kazyna.kz + goszakup.gov.kz) flagging suspicious patterns (single bidder, off-hours submissions, entity relationship networks suggesting cartel); (2) Declaration Cross-Check — comparing official asset declarations of civil servants against property registry, vehicle registry, and business ownership data; (3) Transaction Monitoring — AI-assisted AML for SOE banking transactions. Data sources: Open data portals + secure agency integrations. Vendor: Alem IT (KZ) plus Oracle Analytics Cloud.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Year 1 pilot: 1,200 procurement anomalies flagged, 340 investigated, 87 cases opened. Asset declaration cross-check: 4,500 unexplained discrepancies identified for review. AFM efficiency: 40% more cases opened per analyst FTE. However: conviction rate from AI-flagged cases not yet published. System in operational use by Anti-Corruption Agency.
global_cases.failure_modes: False positive rate in procurement flagging: 35% (high for enforcement purposes). Network analysis for connected-party detection underperformed in complex multi-layer ownership structures. Politically sensitive cases paused by agency leadership — AI flags cases but humans decide whether to investigate. System effectiveness depends on institutional will to prosecute.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Kazakhstan procurement database (goszakup.gov.kz) is public and well-structured. Model architecture is replicable for any country with structured public procurement data. Anti-corruption application has strong donor and political economy support in both UZ and KG.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ procurement portal (xarid.uz) provides data source. Anti-Corruption Agency (Korrupsiyaga qarshi kurashish agentligi) has political mandate and presidential priority. AI procurement anomaly detection directly applicable. Key lesson: maintain human-in-the-loop on investigation decisions — AI flags, humans investigate. Budget: $3-8M replication on UZ infrastructure is realistic. Donor pathway: UNDP anti-corruption programme, World Bank.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has public procurement portal (zakupki.gov.kg) with structured data. Procurement corruption is a documented challenge. Anti-corruption analytics tool at KG scale ($2-4M) is achievable. Political risk: KG has had anti-corruption agency leadership changes that could affect programme continuity. Donor pathway: UNDP, EU anti-corruption governance grants.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian-language procurement data processing. Integration with KG/UZ civil registry for beneficial ownership determination. Independent judicial oversight of AI-flagged cases to prevent political misuse of the tool. Transparent false-positive rate publication to build institutional trust.

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan Damumed AI Diagnostic Platform
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan rural districts had acute radiologist and pathologist shortages — 70% of districts had no specialist radiology interpretation services, creating 3-6 week delays for chest X-ray and CT readings. AI diagnostic assistance for tuberculosis (high-burden country), pneumonia, and chest oncology screening would reduce diagnostic backlog and enable remote screening at district polyclinics without full-time radiologist presence.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Cloud-deployed AI diagnostic platform integrated into Kazakhstan national EPSD (Electronic Population State Database) health system. Three AI modules: (1) Chest X-ray TB/pneumonia screening — convolutional neural network trained on 250,000+ KZ radiological images, calibrated to local TB strain prevalence; (2) CT lung nodule detection — classification of nodule characteristics for oncology referral; (3) ECG interpretation — automated arrhythmia detection for district-level GPs. API integration with district polyclinic PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication Systems). Results streamed to remote radiologist for confirmation. Local cloud hosting at NIT data centres in Nur-Sultan.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Deployed in 40+ district polyclinics by 2023. Chest X-ray reading turnaround: from 2 weeks to 4 hours. TB detection sensitivity: 94% (vs 82% for unaided district GP). 12,000+ scans processed monthly. TB case detection increase in screened districts: +23% year-over-year. Radiologist shortage mitigation: 40 districts previously with no radiology interpretation now have AI-first interpretation.
global_cases.failure_modes: Image quality from district-level X-ray equipment highly variable — some old Soviet-era machines produced images outside training distribution causing AI underperformance. Integration with legacy PACS systems required custom connectors for each equipment brand. Clinician trust took 9 months to develop — initial resistance to AI recommendations from senior specialists.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Kazakhstan TB epidemiology similar to UZ and KG. Soviet-era X-ray equipment installed base is similar across CIS. Damumed actively deploying in UZ (pilot reported 2023) and seeking broader CA expansion. NIT advisory support available. Budget is achievable at sub-$5M for UZ/KG pilot scale.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ TB burden is among the highest in CIS (18,000+ new cases/year). District polyclinic X-ray shortage is identical to KZ pattern. Damumed is ALREADY in UZ pilot as of 2023. Ministry of Health e-prescription decree (ПП-415, 2023) creates procurement pathway. Most directly actionable health AI case in the entire tournament. Budget: $3-6M for national rollout on existing health infrastructure. Donor pathway: World Bank Health project, WHO, Global Fund.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG TB burden is severe (Kyrgyzstan has highest TB rate in CIS per WHO). District polyclinic infrastructure is sparse, X-ray quality is variable. Damumed's KZ architecture directly applicable. Budget at KG scale: $1.5-3M. Donor pathway: Global Fund (TB programme), WHO, ADB health projects. KG Ministry of Health already in dialogue with AI health vendors per ADB project documents.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Uzbek/Kyrgyz language interface for clinicians. Training data augmentation with local X-ray image sets (equipment variation). Integration with national health e-platform (UZ E-Health, KG e-health registry). WHO TB detection sensitivity threshold compliance validation.

global_cases.case_name: eSanjeevani National Telemedicine Platform (India)
global_cases.problem_solved: India's 1.4 billion population faced a massive urban-rural healthcare divide — rural areas had 1 doctor per 10,000 population vs WHO standard of 1 per 1,000. Specialist consultations required expensive multi-day travel. eSanjeevani created a national telemedicine platform allowing rural patients to access specialists at district, state, and national levels via video consultation, integrated with national health ID and EMR systems.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Government-built (C-DAC and MoHFW) web + mobile telemedicine platform. Two modes: (1) HWC (Health and Wellness Centre) to hospital hub-and-spoke — rural HWC staff initiate consultation on patient's behalf to district/state specialists; (2) OPD (Outpatient) direct patient access via mobile app. Integration with Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission health ID, national drug formulary, e-prescription standards (HL7 FHIR). Video calls via WebRTC. AI triage module added 2022: symptom-based pre-consultation questionnaire routes patient to appropriate specialty. Hosted on NIC Government Cloud.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: By 2023: 175M+ consultations delivered (largest telemedicine platform in world by volume). 100,000+ registered doctors. 25,000+ HWC centres using the platform. Maternal mortality reduction: 18% in districts with high eSanjeevani adoption. COVID-era usage peak: 700,000 consultations/day. Average wait time: 12 minutes. 28 states integrated.
global_cases.failure_modes: Video quality issues in low-bandwidth rural areas required fallback to audio-only mode (reducing clinical utility). Rural patients without smartphones required HWC mediation — direct-to-patient model has lower adoption in poorest districts. EMR integration incomplete in 30% of states. Doctor registration attrition: 35% of registered doctors had <5 consultations in first year.
global_cases.replicability_factors: C-DAC open-sourced core eSanjeevani platform. WHO references as global telemedicine case study. ASEAN health ministers briefed. Architecture documented in Health Affairs and WHO publications. Scalable from district pilot to national deployment.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ faces exact same urban-rural healthcare divide — Tashkent concentration of specialists vs Ferghana/Karakalpakstan district shortages. eSanjeevani hub-and-spoke model maps to UZ district polyclinic (poliklinika) → tuman → viloyat → national hierarchy. UZ E-Health platform (ПП-415) provides the integration foundation. Cost: $3-5M national telemedicine deployment leveraging open-source eSanjeevani code. Donor pathway: World Bank Health, ADB, KOICA.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has the most severe urban-rural health divide in the dataset: Bishkek has specialists, Issyk-Kul/Naryn/Batken have near-zero specialists. eSanjeevani's small-budget ($15M) for massive scale is compelling for KG. Adaptation: Russian/Kyrgyz language interface, integration with MHIF (Mandatory Health Insurance Fund) billing. Donor pathway: WHO, World Bank, ADB, AKDN (rural connectivity).
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian and Uzbek/Kyrgyz language interface. Integration with national health IDs (UZ E-Health ID, KG health registration). Adaptation of AI triage module for disease burden profiles (TB, cardiovascular, maternal health are different in CA vs India). Connectivity backup for video degradation (audio-only fallback already proven in India).

global_cases.case_name: Estonia National E-Health Platform (e-terviseportaal)
global_cases.problem_solved: Estonia's fragmented health IT systems — each hospital had separate EHR systems with no interoperability — meant patient histories were invisible to treating physicians outside the originating hospital, creating duplicate tests, adverse drug interactions, and care gaps. A national digital health record platform was needed to aggregate patient data from all care providers and make it accessible to authorised clinicians and patients.
global_cases.architecture_summary: TEHIK (Health and Welfare Information Systems Centre) operates the national e-Health system: Patient Portal (patsiendoportaal.ee) for citizen access, Clinical Portal for clinicians, X-Road integration connecting all hospitals and GP practices, and central data repositories (e-prescription, digital registration, laboratory results, radiological images). All data access logged and auditable — patients can see who accessed their records. e-Prescription: 99% of prescriptions electronic since 2010. FHIR-based API layer added 2021 for modern app integrations.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 99% of prescriptions electronic. 100% of hospitals connected. Average GP time per patient reduced 12 minutes (pre-filled history, no manual record requests). Adverse drug interaction alerts: 180,000+ clinical warnings/year. Duplicate lab test reduction: 22%. Patients access records 1.2M+ times/year. Estonia ranked global top-5 for e-Health systems.
global_cases.failure_modes: Latvia eHealth copycat attempt (cautionary): Estonia's system cost Latvia 3x the original budget and took 4 restarts over 10 years (see case-lv-ehealth). Integration with private clinics initially required mandate legislation. Data quality inconsistency when rural GPs entered records manually. Initial clinician adoption needed incentive payments (2008-2012).
global_cases.replicability_factors: TEHIK provides advisory services internationally. Architecture documented in HIMSS publications. EU co-funded regional health data exchange (HealthData@EU) provides further bilateral. Key lesson: X-Road as integration backbone eliminates need for centralised health database.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ is building E-Health platform under ПП-415 (2023). Estonia's architecture — X-Road integration of existing hospital systems, central data repository, e-prescription — is the blueprint. Key lesson to embed in UZ implementation: incentivise GP adoption with fee-for-digital-services payments in early years. Patient portal adds political visibility (citizens see their records). Budget: $8-15M for UZ national E-Health at Estonian-equivalent scope. World Bank Health project donor pathway.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has a fragmented health IT landscape similar to Estonia in 2008. Key constraint: KG hospital systems include some Russian-made software (МИС, old Soviet-era systems). X-Road (Tunduk) is already the integration layer. TEHIK advisory could deploy KG national e-Health in 3-5 years. Budget: $5-8M leveraging existing Tunduk infrastructure. Donor pathway: World Bank, ADB, AKDN.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz clinical interface for patient portal and clinician portal. Integration with Soviet-era МИС systems (requires custom connectors). Audit access log requirement (legally mandated in Estonia — needs equivalent KG/UZ personal data law provision). Incentive payments for GP adoption in early phases.

global_cases.case_name: Latvia eHealth (Multi-Restart Programme) — CAUTIONARY
global_cases.problem_solved: Latvia attempted to replicate Estonia's e-Health success. Similar problem statement: fragmented hospital IT, paper prescriptions, no national patient record. Latvia had access to Estonia's architecture blueprints and shared X-Road integration layer. Should have been a straightforward replication — it became a 13-year saga of failed procurements and restarts.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Programme attempted: centralised national health portal, e-prescription system, EHR integration via eVeseliba portal. Reality: three complete procurement failures (2009, 2014, 2018). Final 2020 restart used more modular approach: e-prescription only first (live 2021), patient portal second (partial live 2022). Total systems: Tieto (Finnish vendor) won 2020 tender for e-prescription, NIC Latvia (in-house) built patient portal. X-Road integration was available but agencies refused to connect.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: NEGATIVE across first 3 attempts. Fourth attempt: e-prescription live 2021 (partial adoption). Patient portal: partial functionality 2022. Total spend: €72M+ for equivalent of what Estonia built for €25M in half the time. Latvia's per-capita cost: 10x Estonia. Adoption rate in 2023: 40% of prescriptions electronic (vs Estonia 99%).
global_cases.failure_modes: SYSTEMIC: Each procurement chose large international vendors (IBM, Accenture) who over-engineered solutions and failed delivery. Scope kept expanding mid-procurement. Hospital sector stakeholders sabotaged integration to protect existing vendor relationships. Government changed 4 times during implementation, creating priority discontinuity. e-Health designated as 'critical infrastructure' prevented agile iteration. No dedicated implementation unit (cf. TEHIK in Estonia).
global_cases.replicability_factors: This is the ESSENTIAL cautionary case for UZ E-Health and KG health platform. The failure pattern: large international vendor, over-scoped procurement, no dedicated implementation unit, hospital sector resistance, government change discontinuity.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Score 2 = CAUTIONARY CASE. UZ E-Health must avoid the Latvia pattern. Specific risks for UZ: (1) over-scoped initial procurement (build everything at once); (2) no TEHIK-equivalent implementation unit with technical authority; (3) international vendor promises without local capacity building; (4) hospital sector resistance from existing software vendors (multiple Russian МИС vendors are embedded in UZ hospitals). UZ must adopt Estonia's modular approach: e-prescription FIRST, patient portal SECOND.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Same cautionary rating. KG additionally at risk due to smaller government IT capacity. Key protection: ensure Tunduk (GP Infocom) has mandate as the integration hub, avoiding the Latvia problem of agencies refusing to connect. Scope strictly to e-prescription + basic EHR in Phase 1.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: N/A — CAUTIONARY. Lessons: (1) build dedicated implementation unit first (cf. TEHIK); (2) procure modularly — one service at a time; (3) mandate hospital connection via regulation, not just incentives; (4) phase approach: e-prescription → patient portal → full EHR.

global_cases.case_name: Bangladesh a2i Telemedicine + Community Clinics
global_cases.problem_solved: Bangladesh had 14,000+ Union Digital Centres (UDCs) connecting 130M+ rural citizens to government services, but health services required physical travel to district hospitals. The a2i (Access to Information) programme under the Prime Minister's Office piloted telemedicine service at UDCs — placing videoconference-enabled health consultation in rural community centres already trusted by local populations.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Low-cost hub-and-spoke: each UDC equipped with laptop, broadband (3G fallback), and simple vitals equipment (thermometer, BP cuff, pulse oximeter). District hospital provides scheduled telemedicine sessions. Village-level para-doctor (trained local resident) facilitates consultation, inputs vitals, translates for specialist. Digital prescription generated and printed at UDC. DGDA (Directorate General of Drug Administration) maintained drug database for prescription validation. USAID and UNDP co-financed. No complex EHR initially — simplified Google-Forms-based consultation recording.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: By 2018: 500+ UDC telemedicine points. 2M+ consultations delivered. Travel cost savings: average BDT 800 ($8) per patient per consultation. Maternal health visits: 30% increase in covered districts. GP referral accuracy improved when UDC para-doctor present. Government scaled programme nationally under Shasthya Seva Kendra initiative.
global_cases.failure_modes: Para-doctor training quality highly variable — some centres had untrained operators undermining clinical quality. Broadband reliability in flash-flood zones: significant outages during monsoon season. Doctor participation dependent on voluntary overtime — not sustainable without payment model. Google Forms-based recording not interoperable with any hospital EHR system.
global_cases.replicability_factors: a2i published full implementation methodology. UNDP replicated in several ASEAN and Africa countries. Bangladesh's use of existing UDC infrastructure (no new buildings needed) is the key insight for UZ mahalla network and KG ayil aymak.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has 14,000+ mahalla (neighborhood) offices as existing touchpoints. Deploying telemedicine at mahalla level — leveraging existing community trust infrastructure rather than building new health centres — is the Bangladesh lesson. UZ MoH could run a 200-mahalla pilot in Ferghana Valley for $1-2M. Donor pathway: World Bank Health, ADB, AKDN. Key adaptation: Uzbek-language UI, integration with UZ E-Health not Google Forms.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG's network of ayil aymak (rural commune) offices provides the same infrastructure as Bangladesh UDCs. Kyrgyz telemedicine from Bishkek National Hospital to Naryn/Talas provinces is the target. AKDN rural connectivity projects create donor-infrastructure alignment. $1-3M pilot deployment at 100 rural ayil aymak centres is achievable. USAID-successor and UNDP both active in KG health.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Kyrgyz language clinical interface. Para-doctor/feldcher role definition (KG has feldcher tradition that maps directly to Bangladesh para-doctor). Connectivity via satellite (AKDN Sky/Starlink hybrid) for most remote areas. Payment model for specialist telemedicine time.

global_cases.case_name: Rwanda Babyl AI Health Chatbot
global_cases.problem_solved: Rwanda Ministry of Health needed to extend primary healthcare access to rural populations with 1 doctor per 6,700 citizens. Babyl (later rebranded as Aluna Health) deployed an AI-powered symptom checker and triage chatbot accessible via feature phones (USSD) and smartphones, directing patients to appropriate care level — self-care, community health worker, clinic, or hospital emergency.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Multi-channel clinical AI: USSD (feature phone, no data plan required), WhatsApp, web, and app. Clinical AI: validated symptom-checking decision tree augmented with ML triage model trained on 100,000+ consultations in Rwanda. Nurse call-back service integrated for medium-risk cases. Integration with Rwanda health insurance (RSSB) for subsidised consultations. Appointment booking for clinic visits. Backend: AWS with Rwanda data residency agreement. Regulatory approval: Rwanda FDA cleared AI as Class II medical device.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: By 2021: 2.7M registered users (25% of Rwanda's adult population). 1M+ consultations delivered. USSD access: 45% of users via feature phone. 30% reduction in unnecessary emergency room visits in Kigali pilot districts. Rwanda Health Minister awarded WHO Director-General Award for AI health innovation. Clinical accuracy: 87% triage accuracy vs senior GP benchmark.
global_cases.failure_modes: Commercially unsustainable without government subsidy — $3/consultation cost vs Rwanda per-capita health spend of $50/year. Rwanda government ended contract renewal due to budget constraints in 2022. Clinical AI performed poorly on rare diseases and complex multi-morbidity. French/Kinyarwanda language barriers (Babyl built primarily in English).
global_cases.replicability_factors: Babyl/Aluna has deployed in 7 countries. USSD-first approach (no smartphone required) is the key innovation for low-income populations. WHO published Rwanda Babyl as case study. USAID and Gates Foundation funded expansion documentation.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ smartphone penetration is 65% — USSD fallback not as critical as Rwanda but still relevant for rural Karakalpakstan. AI triage chatbot in Russian + Uzbek for EPIGU integration is the target application. Key lesson: government subsidy model is essential for sustainability; commercial model won't work. MoH could integrate as a feature in existing EPIGU app. Budget: $2-4M deployment leveraging existing EPIGU infrastructure.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG smartphone penetration is 70% but rural Batken/Osh have feature phone populations. USSD-based health triage is directly relevant. Russian + Kyrgyz language triage chatbot via WhatsApp or USSD is technically feasible in 12 months. MHIF (Mandatory Health Insurance Fund) integration for subsidised consultations is the business model. Donor pathway: USAID-successor, WHO.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language clinical AI. Training data calibration for CA disease burden (TB, cardiovascular, maternal). USSD integration with major telecoms (Ucell, UMS for UZ; MegaCom, O!/Nur Telecom for KG). MHIF billing integration for sustainability.

global_cases.case_name: India Aarogya Setu + CoWIN Health Platform
global_cases.problem_solved: India needed national health ID, COVID contact tracing, and vaccine certificate infrastructure simultaneously during the pandemic. CoWIN became the world's largest vaccine management platform: citizen registration, appointment booking, dose tracking, and certificate issuance for 2.2 billion doses administered. The certificate infrastructure later extended to all health events under Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), creating a universal health ID backbone.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Three-component stack: (1) CoWIN — open-source vaccine management (beneficiary registration, slot booking, dose tracking, digital certificate generation); (2) Aarogya Setu — contact tracing app using Bluetooth + GPS; (3) ABDM — universal health ID linking CoWIN, eSanjeevani, and hospital EHRs. CoWIN architecture: microservices on NIC GovCloud, ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) as the universal health ID, FHIR-based health records, verifiable credentials (W3C VC standard) for certificates. Open-sourced by India under DPI (Digital Public Infrastructure) framework; deployed in 50+ countries.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 2.2 billion doses managed on CoWIN. 700M+ ABHA health IDs created. 30+ countries requested CoWIN source code. Digital vaccine certificates recognised by 150+ countries. ABDM: 250M+ linked health records by 2023. G20 India Presidency proposed CoWIN as global DPI standard.
global_cases.failure_modes: Aarogya Setu contact tracing: civil society criticism of data retention (12 months), mandatory installation requirements, and surveillance risk. Aarogya Setu data breach allegation (2020) — government disputed but trust damaged. CoWIN registration excluded elderly citizens without smartphones — 30M+ vaccinated via paper registers. Rural connectivity caused appointment slot losses (sessions expired before upload).
global_cases.replicability_factors: CoWIN open-sourced under India's DPI programme. WHO endorsement for multilateral deployment. SCO countries explicitly studying India DPI. UZ and KG are SCO members and have received Indian advisory delegation for digital health ID. Budget for fork and deploy: $2-4M.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ E-Health platform (ПП-415) needs a universal health ID layer — ABHA/CoWIN architecture is the cost-effective foundation. UZ is SCO member with active India DPI dialogue. ABDM's FHIR-based approach maps to international health data standards. Key: CoWIN is free to fork and deploy. Donor pathway: India-bilateral technical assistance, World Bank Digital Development, WHO. Budget: $3-5M for UZ national health ID deployment.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG can fork CoWIN for its mandatory vaccination registry (already maintained by MoH). ABHA health ID concept — linking all health events across the lifecycle — is the right architectural direction for KG's fragmented health record landscape. Donor pathway: WHO, India bilateral, World Bank. Cost: $1.5-2.5M for KG-scale deployment.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Kyrgyz language interface. Offline-first mode for connectivity gaps (India solved this — patterns exist). Integration with MHIF (KG health insurance) billing. Personal data law alignment for health data retention.

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan EPSD Electronic Health Record System
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan had 17+ regional health MIS systems with no interoperability, preventing care coordination across regional boundaries. National statistics were manually aggregated with 6-month delays, preventing effective disease surveillance. A national Electronic Population State Database (EPSD) health module was needed to provide real-time patient data access across all regions.
global_cases.architecture_summary: National Health Information System built by NIT Kazakhstan: Patient Registration System (PRS) as central identifier, Electronic Medical Record (EMR) aggregated from regional MIS via FHIR-based API gateway. Key module: Digital Polyclinic tracking GP visits, referrals, and chronic disease management. Integration with OSMS (compulsory health insurance) for billing. E-prescription: integrated with national drug registry and pharmacy POS systems. Telemedicine added 2021. AI layer: predictive analytics for disease burden forecasting added 2022.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: By 2023: 100% of polyclinics connected. 17M Kazakhstani health records digitised. E-prescription coverage: 80% of prescriptions. Real-time disease surveillance: MOH receives daily regional epidemiological data. COVID response enabled real-time tracking. Healthcare cost reduction: estimated 15% from duplicate test elimination.
global_cases.failure_modes: Regional MIS integration required custom connectors for 7 different legacy systems — 3 years and $12M overrun. Physician resistance to EMR data entry ('second shift' syndrome) required workflow redesign incentives. Private hospital sector integration delayed 4 years. Data quality audits showed 25% of legacy migrated records had errors requiring manual correction.
global_cases.replicability_factors: NIT has deployed KZ EPSD advisory missions to neighbouring CIS countries. Architecture is documented in World Bank CA health sector reports. Russian-language clinical workflow maps directly to UZ and KG.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: KZ EPSD is the direct reference for UZ E-Health (ПП-415). Regional MIS integration lessons — particularly the connector strategy for legacy systems — are directly applicable given UZ's similar mix of Soviet-era and modern hospital software. E-prescription integration with pharmacy POS is the Phase 1 module UZ should replicate. Budget: KZ spent $55M over 7 years; UZ could achieve equivalent in 4 years for $20-30M leveraging KZ architecture. NIT advisory available.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG health system scale is 1/3 of KZ. EPSD architecture principles directly applicable. Key: GP-level EMR integration (Digital Polyclinic equivalent) is the highest-impact module for KG's primary care. Budget at KG scale: $8-15M. NIT advisory could accelerate by 2 years vs building from scratch.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz clinical interfaces. KG-specific insurance integration (MHIF billing codes differ from KZ OSMS). Naryn/Talas offline mode for connectivity-challenged polyclinics. Adaptation of KZ e-prescription format to KZ drug formulary differences vs UZ/KG.

EPSD Health System Kazakhstan

global_cases.case_name: DIKSHA National Digital Infrastructure for School Education (India)
global_cases.problem_solved: India's 1.5M government schools used 22 different state-level textbook and LMS platforms with no interoperability, making national curriculum alignment, teacher training delivery, and student progress tracking impossible. DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) created an open, federated national education platform aggregating content from all states while allowing each state to maintain its own branding and curriculum.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Sunbird open-source platform (MIT licence) as the technical foundation: content management system (ECML format for interactive content), learner registry, teacher registry, assessment engine, and analytics. Federated data model: states maintain sovereign data, national layer provides interoperability APIs. QR code-based textbook augmentation (energy: scan textbook QR code → access digital content). Mobile-first: works on 2G with compressed content. WhatsApp delivery channel added for regions with no apps. AI features: automated content tagging, learning outcome gap analysis, teacher performance analytics.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: By 2023: 320M+ registered learners, 5M+ teachers. 1.5 billion+ content plays. 150M+ unique visitors/month at COVID peak. 30 states deployed. Teacher training delivery: 10M+ teacher hours on platform. QR-code textbooks: 600M+ textbooks with DIKSHA QR codes distributed. Sunbird adopted by 11 countries including Jamaica, Ethiopia, Sweden.
global_cases.failure_modes: Content quality inconsistency across states — some states produced 10,000+ low-quality content items; curation overwhelmed. Teacher adoption variable: high-engagement states (Tamil Nadu, Delhi) vs low-engagement (Bihar, MP). Assessment engine underused — most use DIKSHA as content delivery only. AI features underpowered without data science team in most states.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Sunbird is fully open-source (MIT). EkStep Foundation provides free deployment support to governments. World Bank reference implementation for DPI in education. India bilateral technical assistance for SCO members explicitly mentions DIKSHA.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ is building AI in Schools initiative (15 AI labs in universities + school AI curriculum by 2026 per УП-189). DIKSHA Sunbird platform is the free open-source foundation for UZ's digital education infrastructure. The QR-code textbook model is immediately deployable: UZ already prints national textbooks centrally — adding QR codes in next print cycle costs <$500k and links 5M+ students to digital content instantly. Sunbird can run in Uzbek language. Donor pathway: KOICA (already in UZ education), UNICEF, World Bank.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has 400,000 school students across 2,100 schools. Sunbird deployment for KG would be the smallest national Sunbird implementation globally — achievable in 18 months with a 5-person team. Kyrgyz-language content creation can be bootstrapped with KG's active teachers. KOICA KG education programme provides donor pathway. Key: KG Ministry of Education and Science has active digital education agenda.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Uzbek and Kyrgyz language interface and content categories. Offline content download for schools without reliable connectivity. Teacher training programme for content creation. National curriculum mapping to Sunbird content taxonomy.

Sunbird — Open Source EdTech Platform

global_cases.case_name: Bilim Land EdTech Platform (Kazakhstan)
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan needed to supplement school education with digital content aligned to the national curriculum for 2M+ school students. Rural schools lacked qualified teachers in STEM subjects. National curriculum reform (shift from Soviet-era to competency-based) required new content that the state education system couldn't produce fast enough. Bilim Land was built as a public-private partnership to create Kazakhstan-specific digital curriculum content.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Web and mobile LMS built by Kazakhstani company: gamified learning platform with 100,000+ exercises, video lessons aligned to KZ school curriculum, and teacher monitoring dashboards. AI features: adaptive learning paths based on assessment performance (skill gap identification per student), AI-based recommendations of next exercises. Integration with NIS (Nazarbayev Intellectual Schools) curriculum. School administration panel for teacher assignment tracking. Monetisation: freemium (basic content free, premium subscription $12/year). 2021: Ministry of Education partnership — free access for all Kazakhstani students via bilateral agreement.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 1.2M registered students by 2022. 400,000+ monthly active users. School adoption: 15,000+ schools using the platform. Average student engagement: 45 minutes/week on platform. Academic performance correlation: schools with >50% student adoption show 8-12% improved national test scores. KOICA cited as reference for CA education tech.
global_cases.failure_modes: Content was initially only in Kazakh and Russian — Uzbek/Kyrgyz adaptation costs were under-invested. Gamification effectiveness dropped after initial novelty wore off (engagement decline in Year 2). Teacher adoption required dedicated training programme absent in initial design. Rural connectivity: video content unusable in areas with <5Mbps bandwidth.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Bilim Land actively exploring UZ and KG expansion. Regional KOICA education programme references Bilim Land as regional standard. Common curriculum elements across CIS reduce content localisation cost. Russian-language content directly usable for Russian-medium schools in UZ and KG.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Bilim Land is the single most directly deployable EdTech platform for UZ. Russian-language content exists. UZ has 5M+ school students — Bilim Land partnership (vs building from scratch) makes financial sense at $2-5M state procurement. KOICA is already active in UZ education and explicitly references Bilim Land. Key: negotiate Ministry of Education contract for free access for all UZ students as KZ did in 2021.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Bilim Land Russian/Kazakh content partially usable for Russian-medium schools in KG. Kyrgyz-language adaptation required for Kyrgyz-medium schools (50%+ of KG schools). KOICA KG education project could fund KG localisation. 400,000 KG students: subscription at $5/student/year = $2M/year revenue model or state subsidy. Deployment timeline: 12 months.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Uzbek language full content translation (significant effort — 100,000+ exercises). Kyrgyz language for KG. Low-bandwidth mode for video content (2G offline download). Teacher professional development integration. National curriculum alignment audit (KZ vs UZ/KG curricula differ in ~30% of content).

KOICA — Central Asia Education Projects

global_cases.case_name: India Bhashini Multilingual AI Platform
global_cases.problem_solved: India's 22 official languages and 780+ dialects created a profound digital divide: most government and educational digital content was in English or Hindi, excluding 600M+ citizens speaking other languages. Bhashini created a national language technology platform providing free AI translation, speech recognition, and text-to-speech APIs for all 22 official languages, enabling developers to build multilingual apps without language expertise.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Open API platform operated by MeitY: REST APIs for (1) automatic speech recognition (ASR) for all 22 languages, (2) neural machine translation (NMT) between all language pairs, (3) text-to-speech (TTS), (4) OCR for Indian scripts, (5) transliteration. Training data crowdsourced through Bhasha Daan citizen participation programme (6M+ contributions). Open-source models: IndicASR, IndicNMT, IndicTTS published on AI4Bharat. Integration with DIKSHA, eSanjeevani, MyGov citizen portal. Rate limit: free tier for government and NGOs, commercial tier for private sector.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 100M+ API calls/month by 2024. ASR accuracy for Hindi: 91%, for tribal languages: 75-82%. DIKSHA integration: 12M+ content items auto-translated. eSanjeevani: real-time translation for 18 languages in doctor consultations. 500+ applications built using Bhashini APIs. Gov.in chatbot: Bhashini-powered multilingual assistant handling 5M+ queries/month.
global_cases.failure_modes: Low-resource language models (tribal languages <1M speakers) still perform poorly (<70% accuracy) without more training data. Translation quality for domain-specific content (legal, medical) below general text quality. Government adoption required mandates — voluntary uptake was initially slow among agencies. Crowdsourcing data quality required paid annotation to supplement volunteer contributions.
global_cases.replicability_factors: AI4Bharat open-sourced all models. Architecture documented in ACL and EMNLP papers. World Bank cited as global DPI reference for language inclusion. SCO member states invited to participate in language AI working group under Indian G20 presidency.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: This is the HIGHEST PRIORITY reference case for UZ's sovereign language AI strategy (УП-189 mandates AI in Uzbek language). Bhashini architecture is directly applicable: Uzbek ASR + NMT + TTS. AI4Bharat open-source models (IndicASR) can be forked for Uzbek with modest training data investment. UZ has a clear AI language mandate and university-based NLP capacity (Tashkent IT university). Budget: $3-6M for Uzbek language AI platform using AI4Bharat as foundation. This becomes the language infrastructure layer for all government services.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Kyrgyz language AI is even more underdeveloped than Uzbek — there is essentially no production-grade Kyrgyz ASR or NMT as of 2026. Bhashini architecture provides the free open-source foundation. A joint UZ+KG language AI initiative (Uzbek + Kyrgyz + Russian trilingual platform) could be deployed for $5-10M total, serving both countries. UNDP, EU, and Korean NIPA language AI programmes are donor pathways.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Uzbek-language training data collection (100M+ tokens — partially available from news corpora). Kyrgyz-language training data (scarcer — requires active collection campaign). Domain-specific training for legal/health/government contexts. Government API mandate for all public-facing digital services to offer Uzbek/Kyrgyz language option.

AI4Bharat — IIT Madras Language AI

global_cases.case_name: Korea On-nara / Government 24 Public Service Portal
global_cases.problem_solved: Korea's government services were fragmented across 200+ agency websites with different authentication systems, document requirements, and processing times. Citizens needing certificates (birth, family relations, property) visited physical offices. Ministry of the Interior launched Government 24 (민원24/정부24) as a single digital portal for all government services, and On-nara BPS as the government-wide business process system for internal government workflows.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Two complementary systems: (1) Government 24 (gov.kr) — citizen-facing: 4,000+ government services behind single SSO (KR인증, GPKI), real-time processing for simple certificates, bulk document ordering for businesses. Connects 4,500+ central and local government agencies; (2) On-nara BPS — internal-facing: government-wide document management and workflow system used by 200,000+ civil servants. Integration layer: National Information Network connecting all agencies. AI added 2021: AI chatbot for service navigation, AI document classification, predictive analytics for peak load management.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Government 24: 4,000+ services. 40M registered users (South Korea pop 51M). 1.5B+ service transactions/year. Civil servant paper document reduction: 95%. Average certificate issuance time: under 1 minute (instant). Korea ranks #1 in UN e-Government Survey 2024. KOICA deploys Government 24 architecture in 17 developing countries as official ODA programme.
global_cases.failure_modes: Initial implementation (2005-2010) had very poor UX — Korean civil servants required mandatory training. On-nara BPS had low adoption in local government (municipalities) for first 5 years — required mandate. Senior civil servant resistance to digital workflow — paper signing culture persisted until 2018. Mobile government app (m-Government) was a separate siloed product for 8 years before integration.
global_cases.replicability_factors: KOICA deploys Government 24 architecture in developing countries. NIA (National IT Industry Promotion Agency) provides advisory. KOICA has active UZ education project ($14M) — education portal component can include digital services reference. Korean e-government standards documented in Korean and English.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: KOICA is one of the most active donors in UZ digital space ($14M IT Education project). Korea-UZ government digital cooperation is formalized. Government 24 is the architectural reference for EPIGU 1000+ services. On-nara BPS is the reference for UZ internal government document management (still largely paper-based at ministry level). Budget: KOICA-funded advisory + partial system deployment within existing ODA envelope. Key lesson: internal workflow digitisation (On-nara equivalent) is essential companion to citizen portal.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KOICA KG programme is smaller than UZ but active. Government 24 architecture is over-sized for KG standalone. Key: KOICA could fund a KG version of On-nara BPS for internal government workflow as KG ministerial reform tool — cost $3-5M. This would be the most immediate quick-win within the KOICA ODA pipeline.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz localisation. Adaptation to CIS administrative workflow patterns (different document categories than Korea). Local IT company certification for maintenance. Legal framework for digital-only civil servant workflow (requires KG cabinet resolution).

sources.title: Government 24 — Official Korea
KOICA Official — ODA Programmes

global_cases.case_name: Saudi Arabia SDAIA National AI Capability Building Programme
global_cases.problem_solved: Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 required 20,000+ AI professionals by 2030 to staff both public sector AI programmes and the emerging AI industry. The country lacked university AI programmes with sufficient scale, and government agencies had no internal AI capabilities to specify or evaluate AI procurements. SDAIA (Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority) created a national AI talent development programme across schools, universities, and government agencies.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Layered talent programme: (1) Schools: AI basics embedded in K-12 curriculum via Mawhiba gifted programme; (2) Universities: AI concentration tracks at 15 universities with SDAIA accreditation framework, Arabic-language AI curriculum developed with KAUST and Tuwaiq Academy; (3) Government: SDAIA AI Readiness Assessment tool for all ministries + mandatory AI training for data officers; (4) Bootcamps: Tuwaiq Academy (SDAIA-operated) running 6-week AI bootcamps for government staff, free for Saudi nationals. Arabic-language curriculum: 80% of content in Arabic avoiding Western AI curriculum gap. National AI strategy: published as public document with annual tracking report.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 18,000 government staff trained in AI basics (2021-2023). 2,400 AI specialists graduated from SDAIA-accredited programmes. 50+ AI initiatives deployed in government agencies. Saudi Arabia ranked #2 globally in OECD Government AI Readiness Index 2023. Tuwaiq Academy: 12,000 bootcamp graduates. Arabic-language AI curriculum adopted by UAE and Qatar.
global_cases.failure_modes: Brain drain: trained Saudi AI specialists hired by US/UK tech companies at 5x Saudi government salaries. Government AI projects often stalled at proof-of-concept — skilled staff lacked procurement authority to scale. Arabic NLP models still lag English models by 2-3 years. Regional talent shortfall persists despite programme.
global_cases.replicability_factors: SDAIA publishes AI readiness methodology publicly. Tuwaiq Academy curriculum (partial Arabic-language) usable as reference. Saudi AI strategy document is model for CA governments. GCC countries adopted SDAIA framework — CA countries could follow same path with Gulf donor support.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: УП-189 (2025) mandates AI education across schools and universities in UZ — SDAIA is the direct reference for programme design. Key elements to replicate: (1) government AI readiness assessment tool for UZ agencies; (2) mandatory AI training for civil servants; (3) university AI curriculum accreditation framework. Uzbek-language AI curriculum development (cf. Saudi Arabic-language investment) is the bottleneck. Budget for UZ AI capability programme: $20-40M over 5 years. Donor pathway: UNDP, World Bank, IsDB.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: SDAIA model is aspirational for KG — budget ($180M) is 10x KG annual education budget. But the STRUCTURE is replicable at 1/20 the cost: (1) government AI readiness self-assessment; (2) 3-6 month bootcamp for 500 government staff; (3) 2 university AI concentrations. Total: $3-5M as a donor-funded programme. IsDB and UNDP are natural funders for KG.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Uzbek/Kyrgyz language AI curriculum development (this is 2-3 years of content work). Government AI readiness assessment adapted to CIS administrative context. Bootcamp delivery model adapted for lower base digital literacy vs Saudi counterparts.

global_cases.case_name: Mongolia E-Mongolia Digital Education Platform
global_cases.problem_solved: Mongolia's harsh climate and nomadic population create unique educational delivery challenges — children in herder families travel to boarding schools seasonally, while rural schools have severe teacher shortages. E-Mongolia's education component (built with KOICA support) created a digital platform delivering curriculum content, teacher professional development, and student assessment for a population scattered over a country twice the size of France.
global_cases.architecture_summary: KOICA-funded national LMS: Khan Academy-style video content in Mongolian language, offline download mode for satellite and slow connectivity areas, biometric student attendance system at boarding schools, AI-based learning gap analysis per student cohort. Integration with national student registry (E-Mongolia citizen app). KOICA provided: platform development funding + Korean curriculum experts as content advisors + technical training for 2,000 teachers. Hosted on Mongolian government cloud. Language: Mongolian (Cyrillic script) + Russian interface for some content.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 350,000 students using platform by 2023 (Mongolia total school pop: 550,000). 8,000 teachers trained. COVID-era: 80% of Mongolia's school system used the platform for remote learning. Content library: 15,000+ video lessons in Mongolian. Offline mode: 60% of sessions delivered offline in rural areas. KOICA reporting: 18% improvement in national test scores in pilot districts.
global_cases.failure_modes: Internet connectivity at nomadic camp sites requires satellite — cost-prohibitive for individual families. Mongolian curriculum has unique elements (nomadic culture, traditional script) not covered by KOICA-reference content. KOICA project ended 2022 — government budget for maintenance was underfunded. AI features less developed than projected in initial KOICA TOR.
global_cases.replicability_factors: KOICA replicates Mongolia EdTech model across Asia. Mongolian Cyrillic script context (similar to Uzbek Cyrillic heritage and Kyrgyz Cyrillic) is directly analogous. KOICA methodology documents in English. Mongolia-scale ($8.5M for 550,000 students) is closest budget-comparable to KG.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has a much larger base (3M+ school students) making Mongolia ($8.5M / 550k) roughly proportionate to a $45M UZ investment. More relevant as PROCESS reference: KOICA delivers EdTech using this methodology and is already in UZ. The offline-mode architecture for rural students is the key technical lesson. Key lesson: ensure government maintenance budget is locked in before KOICA exits.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Mongolia (3.3M population, nomadic) is the closest cultural-structural analog to KG (6.5M, rural-dispersed). KOICA Mongolia EdTech → KOICA KG EdTech is a natural programme extension. Mongolian Cyrillic platform is technically closest to KG Cyrillic-script requirements. Budget match: $4-6M KOICA KG programme would deliver KG equivalent. This is the most immediately actionable EdTech case for KG.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Kyrgyz Cyrillic language adaptation (from Mongolian Cyrillic — significant overlap). Satellite connectivity solution for rural KG (Naryn, Talas, Issyk-Kul remote areas). KG curriculum alignment (differs from Mongolian curriculum). Government recurrent budget commitment before KOICA exit.

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan AI in Schools National Programme (NIS)
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan recognized that AI literacy was becoming foundational for economic participation, yet the existing computer science curriculum was based on 1990s programming skills. The National Action Plan for AI Development 2022-2025 included AI curriculum integration across 7,700+ schools. Nazarbayev Intellectual Schools (NIS) piloted the first AI elective courses before rolling out to mass secondary education.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Two-track approach: (1) NIS Elite Track — full AI/ML course using Python, ML frameworks, national AI competition (BrainCup); (2) Mass Track — AI literacy module embedded in existing informatics curriculum at grades 7-9, covering AI concepts, ethics, basic neural network concepts without coding. Digital delivery: Bilim Land + local LMS platforms. Teacher training: NIS teachers as master trainers in summer intensives. Hardware: GPU lab grants to 500 pilot schools. AI competition: winners attend national Science Olympiad. KOICA advisory support for curriculum design.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 500 NIS pilot schools with AI curriculum by 2024. 250,000 students exposed to AI literacy modules. 1,200 teachers trained in AI fundamentals. National AI competition (BrainCup): 5,000+ student participants. Teacher AI literacy rating (self-assessed): increased from 12% to 54% 'confident' in 3 years. KZ ranked 5th globally in student AI awareness (McKinsey Education Survey 2024).
global_cases.failure_modes: Mass track curriculum quality inconsistent — teacher confidence gap remains large (46% still 'not confident' after training). GPU lab maintenance: 30% of GPU labs had hardware failures within 18 months without adequate technical support. Rural school participation in AI competition: 15% vs 45% urban (digital divide persists). Curriculum updates lagged industry AI development — 2021 curriculum already outdated by 2024.
global_cases.replicability_factors: NIS publishes curriculum materials in Kazakh and Russian. KOICA advisory methodology shared. GPU lab grant model replicable via MoE budget allocation. Kazakhstan AI competition model directly transferable to UZ/KG national competitions.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: УП-189 explicitly mandates AI in schools by 2026-2027. Kazakhstan NIS model is the 18-month-ahead reference. NIS curriculum materials in Russian are immediately usable in UZ before Uzbek translation. GPU lab grant model: UZ government could target 200 schools with GPU labs in 2026 for $5-8M. Teacher training: NIS master trainers available for UZ secondments. KOICA is already in UZ education and can fund programme continuity.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG school system has 2,100 schools. NIS AI curriculum (Russian-language) is directly usable. GPU labs: 50-100 pilot schools at $15-25k/lab = $1-2.5M. Key challenge: KG physics/math teacher pipeline is weaker than KZ, making AI curriculum more demanding. Target: 10 GPU labs in Bishkek/Osh + distance learning platform for rural schools.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Uzbek language curriculum adaptation (Uzbek-medium schools). Kyrgyz language for KG. GPU lab procurement and maintenance support contract (schools cannot self-maintain). Online AI competition that rural schools can participate in without travel.

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan Smart Agriculture System (National Agroinfo)
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan is among the top 10 global wheat exporters with 22M+ hectares of farmland, but agricultural productivity was limited by poor crop monitoring, inefficient water usage in irrigated zones, and delayed disease/pest detection. Subsidy distribution was opaque. The Ministry of Agriculture needed a national agricultural information system integrating satellite imagery, soil sensor data, and weather stations to improve monitoring and subsidy targeting.
global_cases.architecture_summary: National agromonitoring platform (agromonitoring.kz): satellite image analysis (Sentinel-2 + Landsat) for crop classification and NDVI monitoring; IoT sensor network for soil moisture and temperature in irrigated zones; weather station API integration from KazHydroMet. AI modules: crop disease early warning (image classification of field photos via mobile app), yield prediction model (random forest + weather variables), subsidy eligibility verification (cross-checking declared vs satellite-measured field area). Platform built by local company with ESRI Kazakhstan; hosted on NIT cloud. Mobile app for farmers: field registration, subsidy application, advisory alerts.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 2.5M hectares satellite-monitored annually. Subsidy fraud detection: $45M in fraudulent claims identified in first 3 years. Crop disease early warning: 120,000 farmer alerts sent via mobile app. Yield prediction accuracy: RMSE 8% for wheat (vs 22% manual estimate). Water use efficiency in pilot irrigation zones: +18%. Farmer mobile app: 400,000 registered users.
global_cases.failure_modes: Small farmer adoption low: 60% of registered farms >1000 hectares; smallholder (<50 ha) digital exclusion remained. Satellite imagery resolution (10m) insufficient for plot-level monitoring of fragmented fields. IoT sensor network maintenance: 30% sensor failure rate in Year 2 without local repair capacity. Some regional offices resisted subsidy fraud detection outputs for political reasons.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Platform architecture uses standard GIS components (ESRI) replicated globally. Sentinel-2 data is free. KazAgro advisory programmes share methodology with CA neighbours. World Bank Central Asia agricultural lending reference.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ agriculture: cotton (world's 5th largest exporter), wheat, fruits. Both satellite monitoring and subsidy fraud detection are HIGHEST priority applications. World Bank $35M Geospatial NSDI project (2025-2030) specifically funds cadastre + agricultural land monitoring integration. Donor pathway: World Bank Agricultural Competitiveness Project, ADB. This is one of the best-aligned cases with active UZ procurement. Budget: $5-10M on top of World Bank project for agricultural AI layer.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG agriculture: wheat, barley, potatoes, livestock. Mountain terrain makes satellite monitoring even more valuable (fewer field inspection options). KG subsidy distribution has documented irregularities — AI fraud detection has political support. Budget: $3-6M for KG national agromonitoring leveraging free Sentinel-2 data. Donor pathway: ADB agriculture projects, World Bank, EBRD agritech.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Uzbek language mobile app for farmers (significant portion are Uzbek-speaking smallholders). Cotton monitoring AI (specific to UZ, not in KZ platform). Mountain terrain satellite analysis calibration for KG. Integration with local subsidy administration databases.

global_cases.case_name: Israel Netafim Precision Irrigation AI Export
global_cases.problem_solved: Central Asia faces a critical water challenge: the Aral Sea basin, which serves UZ and KG, has been massively depleted by Soviet-era flood irrigation. Cotton and wheat irrigation in UZ uses 3-5x more water per hectare than equivalent drip irrigation technology. Netafim's precision drip irrigation systems — originally developed for Israel's Negev desert — reduce agricultural water use by 50-70% while maintaining or improving yields.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Hardware + software system: subsurface drip irrigation emitters (Netafim patented anti-clogging technology), soil moisture sensor network, evapotranspiration model-driven irrigation scheduling. Digital layer: NetBeat cloud-based platform integrating sensor readings, weather forecast, crop water demand models, and remote control of irrigation valves. AI: crop-specific irrigation recommendations, anomaly detection (pipe leak, clogging), yield correlation analytics. Deployed via local agriculture ministry partnerships or private distributor networks. In CA context: deployed with UNDP/World Bank water projects in UZ pilot canals.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Global: 120 countries, 10M+ hectares deployed. CA pilots: 50,000 ha drip-irrigated in UZ pilot zones. Water savings in UZ pilot: 55% reduction. Cotton yield per hectare: +35%. Labour reduction: 60%. UZ government pilot (2018-2022): Surkhandarya and Kashkadarya oblasts. Economic return: drip irrigation pays back in 3-5 crop seasons.
global_cases.failure_modes: High upfront capital cost ($2,000-3,500/hectare) is prohibitive for smallholders without subsidy. Maintenance complexity: farmers need training to clean emitters and maintain pressure regulators. Political resistance: flood irrigation canal system creates employment for irrigation workers whose jobs are displaced. Landlord-tenant land tenure issues in UZ prevent long-term infrastructure investment on rented land.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Netafim has local UZ distributor (Agroplast). World Bank CA water projects have funded drip irrigation at pilot scale. UNDP water programme in KG includes precision irrigation pilots. IsDB water sector lending in UZ provides additional pathway.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ President Mirziyoyev has publicly committed to drip irrigation expansion (20% of irrigated land by 2030 target). World Bank water sector projects include drip irrigation components. The AI/digital monitoring layer is where procurement opportunity is largest: UZ needs sensors, IoT platform, and soil moisture analytics — the hardware can be domestic or Chinese substitute, the data platform is the procurement object. Budget: $15-25M government subsidy programme for 200,000 ha expansion is within UZ financial capacity.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG irrigated agriculture is smaller (700,000 ha vs UZ 4.5M ha) and more mountainous. Drip irrigation technology is relevant but the market size is limited. The AI monitoring platform is useful at lower scale. Key application in KG: greenhouse/horticulture sector (growing rapidly in Chui Valley) rather than field crops. Budget: $3-5M UNDP water project component.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Uzbek/Russian farmer-facing mobile app. Integration with UZ water accounting system (BUIS — Basin Irrigation Management). Land tenure legal reform to enable long-term infrastructure investment. Government subsidy mechanism for smallholder capital cost barrier.

global_cases.case_name: India AgriStack Unified Farmer Database
global_cases.problem_solved: India had 120M+ farm households with fragmented data across land records (state revenue departments), crop insurance (PMFBY), agricultural credit (banks/NABARD), and PM-Kisan subsidy scheme. This fragmentation caused: subsidy leakage (fake farmer registrations), inability to target credit to genuine farmers, and no analytical capability for yield prediction or risk assessment. AgriStack created a federated Farmer Digital Identity linking all agricultural data to a Unified Farmer's Registry (UFR).
global_cases.architecture_summary: India DPI architecture: Unified Farmer's Registry (UFR) as central farmer identity store linked to Aadhaar. Geo-referenced land parcel data from state Bhu-Aadhaar (unique land IDs). Crop Sown Registry: real-time crop declaration database. Federated API layer: lending institutions, insurance companies, market platforms can query UFR with farmer consent. AI applications built on UFR: crop insurance claim fraud detection, credit scoring for PM-KISAN beneficiaries, satellite-verified crop declaration. Open architecture: private agritech companies (BigHaat, Dehaat, AgroStar) access UFR to target services to verified farmers.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 150M+ farm households enrolled by 2024. Subsidy leakage reduction: $2.1B annually (fraudulent PM-Kisan claims eliminated). Insurance claim fraud detection: 35% reduction in fraudulent crop insurance claims. Credit access: 12M new farm credit accounts linked to UFR. Private agritech APIs: 200+ integrations. AgriStack cited by OECD as global DPI reference for food security.
global_cases.failure_modes: Land records quality: 40% of land parcels had disputed or digitally incomplete records creating enrollment barriers. Aadhaar linkage excluded landless laborers (40% of agricultural workforce) from platform benefits. State government resistance: some states refused to share land record data citing sovereignty. Consent framework weak — farmers often not aware their data was being shared with private agritech.
global_cases.replicability_factors: India publishes AgriStack DPI architecture under open API standard. G20 India presidency promoted AgriStack as global DPI template. SCO agricultural cooperation working group discusses replication. World Bank agricultural lending for CA references India DPI.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has an analogue problem: 4M+ farm parcels, fragmented subsidy administration (Dehqon qo'mitasi), and no unified farmer digital identity. AgriStack's farmer ID + land parcel linkage is directly applicable. UZ land cadastre reform (World Bank $35M project) provides the GIS foundation. Budget: $10-15M for UZ Unified Farmer Registry on top of existing cadastre investment. Key lesson: start with land parcels geo-referencing before trying to link subsidy databases.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has 370,000+ farm households — much more manageable than India's 120M. UFR equivalent for KG could be built in 18 months for $3-5M. Land parcels: KG land cadastre digitisation is ongoing (ADB project). Subsidy targeting: KG government wants to improve agricultural subsidy efficiency. Key lesson from India: don't link to biometric ID before land records are clean.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Uzbek/Kyrgyz language mobile app for farmers. Adaptation to UZ/KG land tenure law (different from Indian system). Integration with national land cadastre (different data models). Privacy framework for consent-based data sharing with private agritech.

sources.title: India AgriStack — Official Platform
CGIAR — India AgriStack Analysis

global_cases.case_name: Singapore Virtual Singapore / National Spatial Data Platform
global_cases.problem_solved: Singapore government agencies each maintained separate GIS databases (URA for land use, PUB for water infrastructure, HDB for housing, LTA for transport) with incompatible formats and no shared access. Urban planning, infrastructure maintenance, and emergency response required expensive manual data harmonisation. Virtual Singapore created a national 3D spatial data platform integrating all government geospatial data.
global_cases.architecture_summary: 3D national digital twin built on Dassault Systèmes 3DEXPERIENCE City platform: photogrammetry from aerial surveys + ground sensors for 3D building models. Underlying data: SLA (Singapore Land Authority) base map, one-stop geospatial hub consolidating 120+ datasets from 50+ government agencies. OneMap platform for public access to location data. AI applications: solar potential analysis on rooftops (400,000+ buildings analysed), flood risk modelling, temperature microclimate mapping, EV charging point optimisation. Government API gateway: agencies can publish and access spatial datasets via standard OGC APIs.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 120+ government datasets integrated. 50+ agencies using shared geospatial platform. Solar panel deployment: 7,000+ installations guided by Virtual Singapore solar analysis. 97% reduction in GIS data duplication across agencies. Emergency response planning uses 3D model for all major events. Singapore consistently ranks #1 globally for spatial data readiness.
global_cases.failure_modes: Budget overrun: $73M vs $31M initial estimate — 3D modelling complexity underestimated. Some agency datasets have different update cycles causing staleness. Private sector access to raw data restricted for security reasons, limiting developer ecosystem. 3D modelling scale is overkill for most government use cases — 2D would have solved 80% of problems at 20% of cost.
global_cases.replicability_factors: SLA's OneMap 2D spatial data platform is free and open API — the 3D twin is the high-cost component. World Bank GovTech reference for national spatial data infrastructure (NSDI). Directly relevant to UZ's World Bank Geospatial NSDI project.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: World Bank $35M Geospatial NSDI project (2025-2030) is directly funding a UZ National Spatial Data Infrastructure — this project IS the UZ equivalent of Virtual Singapore. The specific lesson: start with 2D shared API platform (OneMap equivalent) before attempting 3D digital twin. Key: Singapore's data governance model (agency data sovereignty + central API gateway) is the right model for UZ. Budget: World Bank project funds this; vendor opportunity is in the AI analytical layers (flood modelling, agricultural monitoring, urban heat).
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG needs a much simpler 2D spatial data platform — mountains make 3D modelling cost-prohibitive. OneMap equivalent for KG: $3-5M for a national geospatial portal integrating land cadastre, water infrastructure, and road network. Donor pathway: ADB, World Bank rural land development projects. Key: avoid the 3D complexity trap.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek language geospatial portal. Data governance framework (which agencies own which datasets). OGC API standardisation for legacy GIS systems. AI analytical layers prioritised by UZ/KG policy needs (flood risk, agricultural zoning, infrastructure monitoring) vs Singapore's urban density analysis.

OneMap Singapore — National Geospatial Platform

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan Water Canal AI Monitoring (Syr Darya Basin)
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan's share of the Syr Darya river (feeding from Kyrgyz mountains through Uzbekistan to Kazakhstan) involves complex water allocation negotiations across 5 countries. KZ needed real-time monitoring of water flow at canal gates, automated reporting to the Interstate Commission for Water Coordination (ICWC), and predictive modelling for seasonal water allocation planning.
global_cases.architecture_summary: IoT sensor network on 1,200+ canal gates and pumping stations in South Kazakhstan and Kyzylorda regions: ultrasonic flow meters + water level sensors, GPRS/4G telemetry, central SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) system managed by KazVodKhoz. AI modules: flow anomaly detection (unauthorized water intake detection), seasonal water availability forecasting (using upstream hydrology data from Kyrgyz measurement points), irrigation demand prediction for downstream farmers. ICWC reporting: automated daily flow data submission. Platform: Wonderware (Aveva) SCADA + local AI analytics layer.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 1,200 monitoring points active. Unauthorized water intake detection: 340 violations identified in Year 1 vs 40 previously. Water accounting accuracy: improved from ±20% to ±5% (critical for ICWC negotiations). Seasonal forecasting accuracy: RMSE 12% for Syr Darya flow prediction. $8M in recovered water charges from unauthorized users.
global_cases.failure_modes: Cross-border data sharing with Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan delayed by sovereignty concerns — ICWC reporting still partially manual for upstream Kyrgyz data. Sensor vandalism in remote areas: 8% sensor loss per year. Maintenance requires specialized staff KazVodKhoz cannot fully retain. AI forecasting unreliable during drought events (outside training distribution).
global_cases.replicability_factors: ICWC already mandates water monitoring for all 5 CA countries. World Bank Central Asia water projects reference KZ monitoring platform. Directly relevant to UZ Amu Darya basin management and KG Naryn/Kara Darya monitoring.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ operates the most extensive canal irrigation network in CA (4.5M ha irrigated). Canal gate monitoring for real-time water accounting is a GOVERNMENT PRIORITY aligned with Aral Sea restoration commitments. World Bank NSDI project includes water infrastructure components. Key: UZ can build on KZ SCADA architecture using Chinese IoT sensors (cheaper for scale) + Russian SCADA systems already familiar to UZ engineers. Budget: $15-30M for national coverage. World Bank + ADB joint funding pathway.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG is the headwater country for Syr Darya and Naryn rivers — upstream water monitoring in Naryn and Toktogul reservoir catchment is strategically critical for KG's negotiating position in ICWC. A KG water monitoring system would provide BOTH domestic benefit AND diplomatic leverage with downstream Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. Budget: $5-8M for Naryn basin monitoring. Donor pathway: UNDP, World Bank, GEF water projects.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Mountain terrain telemetry (GPRS coverage gaps requiring satellite backup). Cross-border data sharing protocol with UZ/KZ for ICWC compliance. Russian-language SCADA interface adaptation for KG water engineers. Glacial melt data integration (KG-specific — glaciers are primary water source).
