global_cases.case_name: India Aadhaar Digital Identity — DPI Foundation
global_cases.problem_solved: India had 400M+ citizens without any government-issued identity document, making service delivery, subsidy targeting, and financial inclusion impossible. Duplicate identities enabled $10B+/year in subsidy fraud. Aadhaar created a biometric digital identity for all 1.4B citizens, enabling a federated digital public infrastructure used by every government and private sector service.
global_cases.architecture_summary: UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India) operates the Aadhaar database: 12-digit unique identity number linked to biometrics (fingerprints x10, iris x2, face). Authentication API: government/private services can verify identity via eKYC API (returns verified demographic data with citizen consent). Virtual ID: privacy-preserving 16-digit temporary ID that doesn't expose Aadhaar number. Data vault: citizen can see every authentication event via MyAadhaar portal. Seeding: Aadhaar linked to bank accounts, SIM cards, government schemes (DBT — Direct Benefit Transfer). Offline verification: XML-based offline verification without internet. ABHA, AgriStack, e-Shram all use Aadhaar as root identity.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 1.4B biometric IDs issued. $33B in direct benefit transfers ($10B/year fraud reduction). Financial inclusion: 80% bank account ownership (up from 35% in 2011). 10B+ authentication transactions/year. Supreme Court ruled Aadhaar constitutionally valid (2018 9-judge bench) with privacy conditions. G20 India promoted Aadhaar as global DPI standard — 50+ countries studying.
global_cases.failure_modes: Authentication failures: 10-15% biometric authentication failure rate for elderly/manual workers (fingerprints worn away). Supreme Court privacy ruling (2018): linked Aadhaar to non-government services declared unconstitutional. Exclusion: 100M+ citizens with poor biometrics cannot authenticate, excluded from services. Data leaks: multiple state government portals leaked Aadhaar data — UIDAI's central database secure but periphery is not.
global_cases.replicability_factors: UIDAI publishes open API specifications. India promotes Aadhaar as G20 DPI standard. World Bank has funded Aadhaar-equivalent projects in 15+ countries. SCO member states explicitly studying Aadhaar for digital ID. UZ MyID and KG GRS are already partial implementations.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ MyID (by Uzinfocom) is already a functional biometric ID system — Aadhaar is the reference for WHAT IT SHOULD EVOLVE INTO: an open API layer that any government service or private sector company can query with citizen consent. The key gap: UZ MyID authentication API is restricted to government use only. Opening it to regulated private sector (banks, insurers, fintechs) with consent framework would unlock massive economic value. Budget: $5-8M for API layer + consent framework on existing MyID. World Bank Digital Economy project.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG GRS biometric ID is the foundation. Expanding to an Aadhaar-equivalent open API for NBKR digital som wallet verification, private bank KYC, and social payment targeting would be the next layer. Budget: $3-5M for API layer. Key lesson: don't mandate Aadhaar-linking to all services (India's Supreme Court overturned that) — keep consent-based.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language enrollment and authentication UI. Consent framework legislation (explicit user consent for each service integration). Elderly/manual worker biometric failure fallback (face recognition + alternate ID path). Open API licensing framework for private sector (separate from government-use API).

global_cases.case_name: France Albert — Government LLM for Civil Servants
global_cases.problem_solved: French civil servants used commercial LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude) for drafting documents, summarising reports, and answering policy questions — but this created data sovereignty issues (government documents sent to US servers) and inconsistent quality (commercial models don't know French administrative law and procedures). Albert is France's sovereign LLM for public servants, hosted on French government cloud.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Albert (DINUM — Interministerial Direction for Digital Government): Mistral-based LLM fine-tuned on French public administration corpus (legal texts, ministerial circulars, administrative procedures). Hosted on HBS (Health and Social Security Base) sovereign cloud infrastructure. Access: API for government developers, chat interface for civil servants via albert.etalab.studio. Open-source: weights published under permissive licence. Data pipeline: regular fine-tuning on new government documents. Use cases: policy memo drafting, legal text analysis, citizen inquiry summarisation, code generation for government developers.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Civil servant pilot (2024): 5,000 users across 15 ministries. Memo drafting time: 35% reduction. Legal text summarisation accuracy: 88% (vs 72% for generic GPT-4). Data sovereignty: 100% France-hosted, zero data leaving EU. Open-source: 200+ government developers contributing. Albert extended to 8 EU governments via EU-Albert collaboration.
global_cases.failure_modes: Hallucination rate for administrative law: 8% — lower than generic models but still requires human review for consequential decisions. Fine-tuning on government corpus created sensitivity about whose administrative 'voice' the model replicates. Compute cost: fine-tuning each new corpus update requires €200k in compute.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Mistral open-source base is globally available. DINUM published full technical methodology. EU-Albert collaboration framework exists. Directly applicable to UZ AI Cluster (УП-189) and KG sovereign AI strategy — a Uzbek/Russian-language government LLM is the most obvious product.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: УП-189 explicitly mandates a UZ AI Cluster — a sovereign Uzbek/Russian government LLM is the PRIMARY USE CASE for that cluster. France Albert is the architecture reference: Mistral open-source base + UZ administrative corpus fine-tuning + UZ sovereign cloud hosting. Key datasets: lex.uz (all decrees), gov.uz (administrative documents), court decisions (sud.uz). Budget: $3-6M for UZ government LLM. New Uzbekistan University AI Cluster is the logical host. This is potentially the highest-value convergent opportunity in the entire tournament.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG needs a Kyrgyz/Russian government LLM for: parliamentary drafting assistance, Tunduk service chatbot, ministry memo drafting. KG could either (1) join the UZ government LLM effort as a bilingual extension (Russian shared, Kyrgyz separate), or (2) build independently. Budget: $2-4M. The joint UZ+KG approach (shared Russian layer + separate national language layers) is more cost-effective.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Training corpus in Russian (legal, administrative) + Uzbek (UZ-specific) + Kyrgyz (KG-specific). Sovereign compute infrastructure (UZ AI Cluster covers this for UZ). Human review protocol for consequential decisions. Open API for government developers with role-based access control.

global_cases.case_name: Singapore PAIR Government LLM Platform
global_cases.problem_solved: GovTech Singapore needed to deploy LLMs to 150,000 civil servants while maintaining data security, preventing hallucinations in official communications, and enabling government-specific customisation that commercial ChatGPT/Claude APIs could not provide. PAIR (Personal AI Assistant for the Public Service) is Singapore's whole-of-government AI assistant.
global_cases.architecture_summary: PAIR platform on Government Commercial Cloud (GCC): RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) architecture — LLM backend (multiple commercial models via API, with data residency on GCC) + government knowledge base (SharePoint, internal databases, policy documents). Guardrails: output scoring for factual claims, automatic citation requirement for claims about policy. Sensitive data handling: classified material NOT allowed in PAIR (ring-fenced), only RESTRICTED and below data. Human-in-the-loop: PAIR outputs are drafts only — officer must review before sending to citizens. Analytics: agency-level LLM usage dashboards for productivity tracking. Open framework: agencies can add their own RAG knowledge bases.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 80,000+ civil servants onboarded by end 2024. Most-used features: policy memo drafting, data analysis, citizen email drafting. Productivity estimate: 20 minutes/day saved per user (SG MDDI report). Policy compliance rate: 94% of PAIR outputs aligned to current government policy (RAG accuracy). Cost: SGD $180/user/year ($135 USD) — economical for government.
global_cases.failure_modes: Hallucination rate on Singapore-specific regulations: 5% (lower than generic models due to RAG). Some agencies bypassed PAIR for commercial ChatGPT (easier UX). Classified data classification confusion — some officers uploaded data above RESTRICTED level. Singaporean dialect (Singlish) handling is poor.
global_cases.replicability_factors: RAG architecture is standard. Singapore publishes PAIR methodology. The key insight: RAG on government knowledge base dramatically reduces hallucination for domain-specific queries. Cost at $135/user/year is achievable even for UZ/KG budgets.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: PAIR architecture is the most directly replicable for UZ government LLM deployment. RAG on lex.uz + gov.uz would create a UZ civil servant AI assistant that can answer questions about decree requirements, administrative procedures, and government services with citation. This is the product that UZ AI Centre should deploy alongside the government LLM infrastructure. Budget: $5-8M for PAIR-equivalent on UZ sovereign cloud with Russian/Uzbek RAG knowledge base.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG civil service (25,000+ staff) would benefit from PAIR-equivalent for: Tunduk service automation, ministry document drafting, parliamentary briefing assistant. RAG on cbd.minjust.gov.kg + gov.kg would create KG-specific knowledge base. Budget: $2-4M for KG government LLM assistant. Can reuse Russian-language layer from UZ implementation.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language RAG knowledge base. Data classification protocol for civil servants. Hallucination detection (output scoring). Open API for ministry-specific knowledge base additions. Human-review mandate for citizen-facing outputs.

global_cases.case_name: UAE Falcon LLM — Arabic Sovereign Foundation Model
global_cases.problem_solved: Arabic-speaking governments and businesses faced a structural disadvantage: all leading LLMs were trained primarily on English (90%+) and performed significantly worse on Arabic language tasks. UAE's Technology Innovation Institute (TII) built Falcon, a sovereign open-source LLM with strong multilingual capabilities including Arabic, to provide an alternative to US-dominated AI models.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Falcon 7B, 40B, 180B parameter transformer models trained on RefinedWeb (5T+ tokens) with Arabic, French, Spanish, and German sub-corpora. Pre-training: 2048 A100 GPUs for 3.5 months (Falcon 40B). Architecture innovations: grouped-query attention, multi-query attention for inference efficiency. Released under Apache 2.0 open-source licence. Arabic NLP benchmarks: Falcon 40B achieved SOTA for Arabic QA, summarisation, and translation. TII provides sovereign compute access for UAE government agencies. Models hosted on Hugging Face with 2M+ downloads.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Falcon 7B/40B: #1 on OpenLLM Leaderboard (May 2023, then surpassed). Arabic NLP tasks: 15-25% better than GPT-3.5 on Arabic benchmarks. Downloads: 2M+ Hugging Face downloads. 15+ Arabic government applications built on Falcon by UAE ministries. Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Egypt adopted Falcon for government Arabic AI. AI sector employment in UAE: +35% (Falcon catalyst).
global_cases.failure_modes: Falcon eventually surpassed by LLaMA 2 and newer models — open-source race means no permanent leadership. Arabic dialect handling: Falcon trained on formal Arabic, poor on Gulf, Egyptian, Levantine dialects. Inference cost for 180B model is prohibitive for most government deployments — 7B model is the practical choice.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Falcon is open-source (Apache 2.0). Architecture documented in arXiv paper. Fine-tuning Falcon for Uzbek + Russian is technically feasible with moderate training budget. UAE TII provides advisory to Gulf states. GCC countries have replicated Falcon-based approaches.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Falcon architecture is the DIRECT MODEL for UZ's sovereign LLM strategy. Falcon-7B base model + fine-tuning on Uzbek administrative corpus would create Uzbek government LLM at $500k-2M compute cost (vs building from scratch). UZ AI Cluster New Uzbekistan University can host. This is the most cost-effective path to sovereign Uzbek AI. SDAIA (Saudi) and TII (UAE) are natural bilateral AI cooperation partners for UZ.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Kyrgyz language fine-tuning on Falcon base is the lowest-cost path to Kyrgyz NLP capability. Kyrgyz corpus is small but sufficient for fine-tuning (KG has 150,000+ pages of Kyrgyz-language government documents). Joint UZ-KG fine-tuning project: shared Falcon base, separate Uzbek and Kyrgyz heads. Budget: $500k-1.5M compute for KG Kyrgyz fine-tuning. UNESCO language preservation grant as potential donor.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Uzbek and Kyrgyz language corpus collection (government documents, Wikipedia, news, court decisions). Fine-tuning infrastructure on sovereign compute. Domain-specific fine-tuning for government use cases (legal, administrative). RLHF (human feedback tuning) with local Uzbek/Kyrgyz language experts.

global_cases.case_name: Estonia Bürokratt AI Government Virtual Assistant
global_cases.problem_solved: Estonia needed a conversational AI assistant for citizens interacting with government services — allowing natural language queries across the full range of 800+ EPIGU-equivalent government services rather than requiring citizens to navigate service menus. Bürokratt provides a federated AI assistant architecture where each government agency hosts its own bot that seamlessly hands off conversations to other agency bots.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Federated AI assistant architecture: each government agency deploys its own Rasa-based conversational AI bot trained on its service domains. The Bürokratt Network connects all agency bots via a central 'Bürobot' router that directs conversations to the correct agency. Estonian language NLP: NLU model fine-tuned on Estonian administrative language. Integration with X-Road: bots can query government registries in real-time during conversation (e.g., 'what is my current pension entitlement?' triggers X-Road query). Open-source (MIT licence): all Bürokratt components published on GitHub.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 15+ government agencies with deployed bots by 2024. 500,000+ citizen conversations/month. Resolution rate: 68% of queries answered without human agent escalation. User satisfaction: 4.2/5. Open-source forks: 5 countries (Latvia, Lithuania, Finland, Ukraine, North Macedonia) deploying Bürokratt-based assistants. Integration with EPIGU equivalent: 200+ services accessible via conversation.
global_cases.failure_modes: Estonian-language NLP performance drops for informal/colloquial language. Federated architecture means agency bot quality is highly variable. 32% escalation to human agents still too high for most agencies. Some services too complex for conversational interface — users prefer structured forms.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Bürokratt fully open-source (MIT licence). RIA provides advisory. Estonian Government is actively promoting Bürokratt for EU and partner country deployment. Russian + Estonian bilingual operation provides model for UZ (Uzbek + Russian bilingual). Most directly applicable AI government product in the dataset.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Bürokratt is the DIRECT reference for UZ EPIGU AI chatbot strategy (CW-007 in convergent windows). The federated architecture — agency bots + central router — matches UZ's distributed ministry structure. Open-source (MIT) means UZ can fork and deploy for $500k-1M (vs $10M+ for custom build). Russian + Uzbek NLP. Integration with EPIGU and X-Road equivalent (UZINTERSTATE) is technically straightforward. RIA advisory available via EGA bilateral programme. This may be the single most actionable AI government case in the entire tournament.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Bürokratt for KG Tunduk services is the direct adaptation: Russian + Kyrgyz bilingual bot, integrated with Tunduk service registry. KG has an even stronger case: smaller number of services means faster deployment. The open-source nature means KG could deploy a working Tunduk AI assistant in 6-9 months for $500k-1.5M. EGA-led EU project in KG (Tunduk modernisation) could include Bürokratt deployment as component.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian + Uzbek NLP training (Uzbek NLP models exist: multilingual BERT variants). Kyrgyz NLP for KG (smaller data requirement but scarcer training data). EPIGU/Tunduk API integration for real-time data queries. Government agency training programme for bot content creation. Human escalation to call centre integration.

global_cases.case_name: Russia Gosuslugi AI Chatbot and Voice Bot
global_cases.problem_solved: Russia's Gosuslugi portal received 150M+ support queries/year overwhelming 20,000+ operators. An AI chatbot + voice bot (IVR) was needed to automate routine queries (service status, document requirements, account issues) and reduce human agent load while maintaining Russian-language quality.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Mintsifry chatbot platform: NLP model (Sber AI FRED-T5 base + fine-tuning on Gosuslugi query corpus), 3-channel deployment (web chat, mobile chat, telephone IVR). Integration with Gosuslugi backend: chatbot can query real-time service status, document requirements, and account information via API. ESIA authentication for personalised responses. Voice bot: ASR (Yandex SpeechKit) + TTS (Yandex TTS) for telephone channel. Fallback: seamless escalation to human agent with conversation context passed.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 45% of support queries handled without human agent (vs target 60%). Human agent load reduction: 8M queries/year automated. User satisfaction with bot: 3.8/5 (lower than human agent 4.6/5). Response time: <2 seconds vs 3-minute wait for human agent. Cost per automated query: $0.08 vs $2.40 human agent.
global_cases.failure_modes: Complex multi-step queries still require human (42% escalation rate for queries about appeals, refusals, and edge cases). Voice bot accuracy for non-standard Russian dialects is lower. Post-2022 sanctions: Yandex SpeechKit facing export control questions for international deployment.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Sber AI models available for Russian-language applications. Architecture is standard NLU + chatbot. Russian-language performance is directly applicable to UZ/KG Russian-medium citizen queries. Post-2022 Yandex/Sber vendor risk for international deployment should be noted.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Russian-language chatbot for EPIGU is immediately deployable using Sber AI or Yandex models (if geopolitical risk acceptable) or open-source alternatives (mGPT, ruBERT). The architecture pattern — NLU + intent detection + EPIGU API queries + fallback to human — is standard. Key: UZ needs Uzbek-language extension alongside Russian. Budget: $2-4M for UZ EPIGU chatbot deploying Bürokratt or this architecture. NOTE: Yandex/Sber dependency creates political risk for EU/World Bank co-funded projects.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG Tunduk citizen-facing chatbot in Russian + Kyrgyz. Sber AI/Yandex components acceptable for Russian layer if KG political risk assessment permits. Open-source alternative (multilingual BERT, mT5) recommended to avoid Russian vendor dependency. Budget: $1.5-3M for KG Tunduk chatbot.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Uzbek NLP extension (not in Russian model). Kyrgyz NLP extension for KG. Avoid Yandex/Sber components in donor-funded projects (use open-source). EPIGU/Tunduk API integration. Human agent escalation with bilingual call centre routing.

global_cases.case_name: Indonesia Satu Data Indonesia Open Data Platform
global_cases.problem_solved: Indonesia's 130+ ministries and 500+ districts each maintained separate data portals with incompatible formats, preventing whole-of-government analytics and creating data duplication. Satu Data Indonesia (One Data Indonesia) Presidential Regulation mandated all government data to be published in open, machine-readable format through a unified national data portal.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Satu Data (data.go.id): national open data portal + mandatory data governance framework. Presidential Regulation 39/2019 mandated: data principals (agencies) to publish all non-sensitive data in standard format, data stewards (provinces) to aggregate regional data, and a national data committee to set standards. Technical stack: CKAN-based data portal, API layer, GIS integration for spatial datasets. AI component: dataset similarity detection (deduplication), automated data quality scoring, metadata completeness checker. Government analytics: Pusdatin (Government Data Centre) builds dashboards on Satu Data feeds.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 35,000+ datasets published by 2024. 350+ data-producing agencies connected. Monthly downloads: 2M+ API calls. COVID: government made real-time case data available via Satu Data 48 hours after pandemic declaration. Developer applications built on Satu Data: 500+. Indonesia ranks 12th globally in Open Data Barometer.
global_cases.failure_modes: Data quality inconsistency: 40% of published datasets have missing metadata. Update frequency: 35% of datasets have last update >6 months ago. Machine-readable mandate partially enforced — some agencies publish PDFs instead of structured data. Inter-agency data sharing still politically contentious for sensitive datasets.
global_cases.replicability_factors: CKAN is free open-source. Presidential mandate model (not voluntary) is the key governance innovation. World Bank open data programmes reference Indonesia. Directly applicable to UZ data.gov.uz and KG data.gov.kg portals.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has data.gov.uz portal but it lacks presidential mandate for mandatory data publication and machine-readable standards. Indonesia's Presidential Regulation 39/2019 is the policy model. CKAN is already deployed in some Central Asian open data portals. Budget: $2-3M for UZ Satu Data equivalent + presidential decree for mandatory agency compliance. World Bank digital governance project donor pathway.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has data.gov.kg in early stages. Presidential mandate model via Kyrgyz Cabinet Resolution could accelerate. Цифровой Кодекс (2025) includes open data provisions. CKAN deployment for KG national data portal: $1-2M. Strong donor interest: EU, World Bank, USAID-successor all fund open government data programmes.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language metadata standards. Mandatory publication decree for all central government agencies. Data steward designation at oblast/oblasts level. AI data quality scoring adapted for Russian-language metadata. Developer community building via hackathons.

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan National AI Strategy 2024-2029
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan needed a comprehensive national AI governance framework — covering procurement standards, ethical guidelines, compute infrastructure, talent development, and regulatory sandbox — to guide $1B+ in planned AI investments through 2029 and position Kazakhstan as the regional AI hub.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Comprehensive strategy document adopted by Cabinet Resolution 2024: six pillars — (1) AI-powered public services; (2) AI regulation and ethics (first CIS AI ethics law); (3) AI talent (50,000 specialists target); (4) AI compute (national sovereign AI data centre); (5) AI ecosystem (Astana Hub AI vertical); (6) AI in priority sectors (healthcare, agriculture, finance). Operational: Digital Kazakhstan 2026 programme included $300M+ AI investment component. KAZNIIISA (National Institute for AI Standards) created as standards body. Annual National AI Report mandated.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Strategy published Q1 2024. Nvidia MoU for 2,000 H100 GPUs signed. National AI Index: KZ ranked #1 in CIS. 15,000 government AI specialists enrolled in reskilling programme. 5 ministerial AI strategy documents published. CIS countries (UZ, KG, AZ) referenced KZ strategy in own strategy drafting.
global_cases.failure_modes: Strategy ambition vs execution gap: most 2024 targets are aspirational without binding accountability mechanism. $1.2B figure includes private sector investment projections that may not materialise. KAZNIIISA understaffed (8 specialists vs 200 needed for comprehensive standards work).
global_cases.replicability_factors: KZ strategy document is public and explicitly offered to CIS neighbours as template. KAZNIIISA has bilateral advisory missions planned for UZ and KG. Most directly relevant for UZ (similarly sized economy at similar development stage 3-5 years ahead).
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ УП-189 AI strategy is 12-18 months behind KZ on implementation. KZ strategy execution details — specifically the KAZNIIISA standards work, the government AI reskilling programme design, and the Nvidia GPU infrastructure deal — are directly applicable to UZ AI Cluster design. UZ should negotiate similar Nvidia MoU for AI Cluster. Budget: KZ $1.2B is 3x UZ expected; UZ should target $300-400M with similar structure. KAZNIIISA advisory for UZ is available.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG National AI Strategy is in drafting stage (announced but not signed as of May 2026). KZ strategy structure is the reference. KG should adapt six-pillar framework to KG scale: scaled-down compute ($10-20M vs KZ $300M), 3,000 specialists target (vs KZ 50,000), 3-sector focus (finance, agriculture, health). UNDP and ADB can fund KG strategy implementation.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: KG: Scale all budget targets by 1/10 vs KZ. Focus on 3 high-priority sectors rather than comprehensive coverage. Avoid KAZNIIISA-scale standards body (KG can reference international standards). Russian/Kyrgyz language AI strategy document (signal of commitment to Kyrgyz-language AI).

KZ AI Strategy adopted — Prime Minister's Office

global_cases.case_name: Kyrgyzstan Tunduk Interoperability Platform Modernisation (EU-Funded)
global_cases.problem_solved: KG Tunduk (GP Tunduk) was established as an X-Road fork in 2018 but ran on X-Road version 6.x while X-Road 7.x introduced REST API support, improved performance, and enhanced audit capabilities. The EU DigiConnect4CA programme funded a Tunduk modernisation to upgrade to current X-Road standards, expand connected agencies, and integrate with the Estonian Government Technology Agency (EGA) ecosystem for future cross-border services.
global_cases.architecture_summary: EGA-led project: upgrade Tunduk security servers to X-Road 7.x, onboard 20 additional government agencies (from current 30 to 50+), deploy X-Road Central Server on KG government cloud infrastructure, integrate Tunduk with KG single digital identity (GRS biometric ID as OIDC provider). EU EU4Digital project provides technical assistance. EGA seconded specialists to Bishkek for 6-month deployment support. Long-term: Tunduk inter-connection with Estonian X-Road instances for potential cross-border pilot.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: ACTIVE — in progress as of Q2 2026. Phase 1 (X-Road 7.x upgrade): completed Q4 2025. Phase 2 (25 additional agencies): 18 onboarded as of May 2026. REST API availability: 40 services available via REST (was 0). UDP digital department (post-April 2026 reorganisation) has designated Tunduk as central integration platform.
global_cases.failure_modes: Reorganisation April 2026 (Mintsifry dissolved → UDP) disrupted project continuity — Tunduk management transferred from Mintsifry to UDP, causing 3-month administrative delay. Some legacy KG agencies using 1C and Soviet-era software cannot provide X-Road-compatible APIs — requires middleware adapter development.
global_cases.replicability_factors: This IS a KG active case. EGA advisory methodology is published. The 6-month specialist secondment model is replicable for other EGA partnerships. Directly relevant to UZ UZINTERSTATE modernisation discussion.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ should negotiate an identical EGA advisory programme for UZINTERSTATE modernisation. The KG model — EGA specialist secondment + EU funding + X-Road upgrade — is directly applicable. UZ's larger scale would require a larger team and longer timeline but same architecture. EU DigiConnect4CA has UZ components. This is an active procurement opportunity for EGA-certified implementation partners.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: This IS the KG case — ongoing. Phase 3 (cross-border integration pilot with Estonia + UZ) is the next procurement. The AI service layer on top of modernised Tunduk (Bürokratt-equivalent bot + open data portal) is the logical follow-on. This is the foundational infrastructure enabling multiple other KG digital services.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: April 2026 reorganisation resolution: confirm UDP's mandate as Tunduk political patron. 1C software middleware adapters for legacy KG agencies. Staff capacity building within UDP for Tunduk long-term operation post-EGA advisory. Procurement of domestic KG IT maintenance contractor for X-Road 7.x stack.

global_cases.case_name: Estonia e-Residency — Digital Governance Export Programme
global_cases.problem_solved: Estonia discovered its digital government infrastructure had global commercial value: entrepreneurs worldwide wanted access to Estonia's business-friendly, EU-compliant digital legal environment without physically relocating. e-Residency gives non-citizens a government-issued digital identity that allows running an EU-compliant company, signing contracts, and accessing EU banking without visa requirements.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Programme: e-Resident digital ID card (government-issued, different from citizen ID but same cryptographic infrastructure). Usage: company registration in Estonia online (3 hours, €200), access to EU banking for e-Resident companies, digital contract signing enforceable under EU law, access to Estonia's digital services as a business. X-Road integration: e-Residents can query Estonian company registry, tax filings. EGA and Enterprise Estonia operate jointly. 1,000+ countries represented. Diaspora-focused: Ukrainians, Russians, Georgians are top applicants.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 110,000+ e-Residents from 180+ countries. 30,000+ e-Resident companies registered. Tax revenue to Estonia: €100M+ from e-Resident companies. ROI: programme cost €7M, revenue €100M+. Diaspora bridge: largest applicant groups include Ukrainians (war-driven), Georgians, Russians (sanctions-driven), Chinese. Top 5 nationalities: Finland, Germany, Russia, Ukraine, USA.
global_cases.failure_modes: 2022: Post-Russia sanctions, many Russian e-Residents had their status reviewed (some revoked if sanctions risk). EU banking access: some EU banks refuse e-Resident company accounts due to AML risk concerns. Physical card delivery to remote countries: 4-6 weeks. Programme has not fully monetised its diaspora bridge potential for bilateral tech diplomacy.
global_cases.replicability_factors: e-Residency model is unique to Estonia's EU membership. For UZ/KG: the DIASPORA BRIDGE application is the key learning — digital identity for diaspora as bridge to motherland services, investment, and business. IT Park Uzbekistan has explored a variant: 'Digital Uzbek' status for diaspora investors.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Full e-Residency model not transferable (UZ is not EU). BUT: the DIASPORA BRIDGE concept — a digital identity for Uzbek diaspora abroad that allows investment facilitation, remote company registration in UZ IT Park, and cultural engagement — is directly applicable. IT Park already has a similar concept in early stages. Budget: $1-3M for UZ Digital Diaspora programme. This is the Lens 5 (Diaspora Bridge) application case.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has 800,000+ workers abroad — diaspora digital bridge could enable remittance reduction (direct to KG government investment platforms vs expensive Western Union), HTP investment facilitation, and skills mapping. Budget: $500k-1.5M. Cultural resonance: 'Digital Kyrgyz' status for diaspora is politically appealing.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language programme. Adapt from EU legal context to UZ/KG investment law. Focus on investment facilitation and skills engagement rather than business registration (EU market access not available). Partnership with KZ and Russia (main diaspora destinations) for programme promotion.

e-Residency — e-Estonia

global_cases.case_name: South Korea Sejong City AI Smart City Platform
global_cases.problem_solved: Sejong was Korea's purpose-built administrative capital (pop 400,000) designed as a testbed for smart city technologies. The government needed to demonstrate commercial-scale deployment of AI urban management systems — autonomous vehicles, AI traffic management, smart energy grid, digital citizen services — to develop exportable Korean smart city products.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Sejong Smart City National Pilot Zone: (1) Autonomous Vehicle Corridor — 7.7km fully AV-ready road with 5G + V2X communications; (2) AI Traffic Management — 300+ adaptive signal intersections, incident detection; (3) Energy Management — AI-optimised community energy storage + building management; (4) City Data Hub — all city data on shared platform, API-accessible; (5) 60-minute delivery service (logistics drone pilot). Government investment: $2.5B in infrastructure over 5 years. KOICA exports Sejong model to developing countries as 'K-Smart City'.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Traffic efficiency: 20% improvement vs comparable Korean cities. AV test fleet: 40 vehicles in daily operation. Energy consumption: 12% below Korean city average. City data hub: 45 agencies sharing data. K-Smart City exports: 22 cities in 14 countries studying Sejong model. KOICA has 4 active K-Smart City transfer projects.
global_cases.failure_modes: Cost: $2.5B for 400,000 people — $6,250/resident is unaffordable for most countries. AV system limited to dedicated corridor — cannot scale to irregular urban grid. Energy management AI requires residential smart meter density that took 5 years to achieve.
global_cases.replicability_factors: KOICA K-Smart City programme transfers specific modules (AI traffic, energy management, data hub) without the full investment. Korean smart city companies (Samsung SDS, LG CNS) active in CA markets. Directly relevant to Tashkent and potential Nurafshan R&D city.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ announced Nurafshan Innovation Centre near Tashkent — a pilot smart city zone. Sejong is the direct reference. Modular adoption: AI traffic ($10-20M) + city data hub ($5-8M) for Tashkent without the $2.5B total investment. KOICA K-Smart City programme is the procurement pathway.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Sejong's scale is totally incompatible with KG. Only the AI traffic module ($3-5M for Bishkek) and city data hub concept are applicable. Score 4: aspirational reference, not practical at KG scale.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Modular adoption: AI traffic + city data hub only. Russian/Uzbek interface. Open-source data hub (FIWARE) vs Korean proprietary stack. No AV corridor — premature for CA markets.

global_cases.case_name: Brazil gov.br Digital Government Portal
global_cases.problem_solved: Brazil's 26 states and federal government each had separate portals (1,400+ .gov.br domains) with different authentication, UX, and service quality. Citizens needed separate logins for federal social security, driving licence, tax filing, and vaccine certificates. gov.br unified all federal services behind a single authenticated portal.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Single Sign-On platform using Login.gov.br: CPF (national ID) + password or biometric authentication. Progressive trust levels: Bronze (self-declaration), Silver (bank-verified), Gold (biometric via Serpro ID). Backend: 1,800+ connected federal services. API: gov.br Digital Certificate API used by 300+ private sector companies for KYC. COVID: digital certificate on gov.br saved programme months of time. AI: personalized service recommendations based on citizen profile and life events (birth, death, employment change). Analytics: SEGES dashboard tracking service delivery times across all agencies.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 155M registered users (Brazil pop 215M). 4,000+ federal services. Average service completion time: reduced 45%. COVID certificate: 350M issued. Portal digital accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA certified. Brazil climbed 20 places in UN e-Government Survey after gov.br launch. Life events personalisation: 80% of users receive relevant service suggestions.
global_cases.failure_modes: State government integration (26 states) lagged federal services by 3 years. Biometric enrollment required in-person for Gold level — excluded 40M rural citizens. Identity theft via CPF-credential theft required multi-factor authentication rollout.
global_cases.replicability_factors: SERPRO publishes technical documentation. Brazil is an active South-South digital cooperation partner. Login.gov.br architecture is directly comparable to UZ MyID evolution path. Brazil's life event personalisation concept is directly applicable to EPIGU.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Brazil's progressive trust level model (Bronze/Silver/Gold) is the right evolution path for UZ MyID — enabling partial access for citizens without full biometric verification while providing full access to those enrolled. The life events personalisation ('proactive government') is the EPIGU evolution UZ officials have stated publicly. Budget: $5-10M on existing EPIGU. UNDP South-South digital cooperation could fund Brazilian-UZ advisory exchange.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Brazil's progressive trust level model is highly applicable to KG where rural biometric enrollment coverage is incomplete. Bronze/Silver/Gold layers allow Tunduk services to be accessible even to citizens without GRS biometric card enrollment. Budget: $3-5M.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language portal. Progressive trust level framework legal decree. Life events API (detecting birth registration, new business registration, etc.) for proactive service suggestions. State/oblast government integration plan from Day 1.

SERPRO — gov.br International Award

global_cases.case_name: Rwanda Vision 2050 AI National Strategy
global_cases.problem_solved: Rwanda, with a population of 13.5M and GDP of $12B, needed to demonstrate that a small, low-income African country could deploy AI at scale in public services. Vision 2050 included AI as a transformative pillar — not for status signalling but to specifically address Rwanda's infrastructure bottlenecks: healthcare access, agricultural productivity, and government service delivery in a mountainous country.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Rwanda AI Policy 2023: government AI use case registry (50+ approved applications across ministries), National AI Lab (University of Rwanda AI Center), Smart Rwanda Master Plan 2024-2029 including AI infrastructure (400GPU compute available by 2025). Applications in production: Babyl health triage, Irembo digital services (see separate cases), agriculture drone monitoring (crop disease detection via mobile image), e-court pilot (AI transcription). Governance: Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority AI ethics committee. Rwanda positioning: 'AI-first small country' as export pitch for other low-income government AI programmes.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 50+ government AI applications deployed or in pilot. 400 GPU national compute. University of Rwanda AI Center: 200+ researchers. Rwanda AI readiness index: ranked #2 in Africa (OECD 2024). Export case: 12 African governments have studied Rwanda AI model. WHO cited Rwanda as global reference for low-income country AI in health.
global_cases.failure_modes: Brain drain: top AI graduates hired by US/UK companies. Budget sustainability: many AI pilots funded by donors with unclear government recurrent budget. Private sector AI adoption lagging public sector. Infrastructure: power reliability (80% electrification) limits AI deployment in rural areas.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Rwanda's AI-first small country model is the direct comparator for KG. Rwanda publishes case studies via Smart Rwanda Initiative. African Development Bank documents Rwanda model for Africa. UNDP and World Bank explicitly cite Rwanda for small-country AI strategy design.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Rwanda is a smaller-economy reference point. Key lesson for UZ: government AI use case registry (50+ approved applications) — UZ MoDT should create a formal registry as governance mechanism. Rwanda's AI ethics committee approach is directly applicable to UZ's AI governance gap.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Rwanda (13.5M, $12B GDP) is the closest population and income comparator to KG (6.5M, $12B GDP). Rwanda's three-year progression from 0 to 50+ government AI applications on small budget ($85M over 5 years) is exactly what KG's AI strategy should target. Rwanda-KG South-South learning programme (via UNDP or World Bank) would be high-value.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Kyrgyz language interfaces (Rwanda is French/English/Kinyarwanda). Adaptation for mountain geography vs Rwanda's hill terrain (similar challenges, different scale). Budget recurrence planning — Rwanda's lesson on donor-exit sustainability is critical for KG.

Smart Rwanda Master Plan 2024-2029

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan Digital Social Protection — e-Otinish Social Registry
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan's social protection system distributed benefits to 3M+ recipients through paper applications, physical window visits, and manually verified income declarations. Targeting errors and fraud cost $300M+/year. e-Otinish (e-Application) digitised social benefit applications and created an AI means-testing system that cross-referenced income from 12 government databases.
global_cases.architecture_summary: e-Otinish platform (Ministry of Labour, ENOF pension fund): online and mobile application for all social benefits (housing, childcare, disability, pension supplements). AI means-testing: income cross-check across tax GNK, pension ENOF, property registry, vehicle registry, banking KQIB data. Application decision: instant pre-decision in 72% of cases; complex cases to officer review. Digital payments: benefits disbursed directly to citizen bank account (IBAN). Fraud analytics: lifestyle-based anomaly detection (declared low income + luxury purchase + overseas travel pattern flagging). Integration with X-Road equivalent (Smart Bridge).
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 4M+ social benefit applications processed digitally. 72% of applications decided instantly via AI means-testing. Social benefit fraud identified: KZT 28B ($60M) in 3 years. Officer workload per application: reduced 55%. Payment disbursement: same-day bank transfer (vs 15 business days physical). Benefit targeting accuracy: 88% of recipients meet actual eligibility criteria (vs 72% pre-digital).
global_cases.failure_modes: Means-testing false positives: 12% of legitimate applicants denied due to data errors in source databases. Rural areas without banking access: 15% of benefit recipients still require cash payment infrastructure. Disability certification: AI cannot verify medical conditions — still requires doctor certification creating bottleneck.
global_cases.replicability_factors: World Bank Social Protection team cites KZ e-Otinish as CIS reference. Russian-language system directly applicable to UZ and KG. UZ World Bank social protection project includes digital registry component.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ social protection reform (World Bank TA) is actively digitising benefits administration. e-Otinish is the direct reference for UZ unified social benefit application (ASA — Agency for Social Assistance). KZ income cross-check architecture maps to UZ MyID + GNK + pension fund integration. Budget: $10-15M. World Bank social protection project is the donor pathway. This is the most directly actionable social protection case in the dataset.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG social protection (UISE — Unified Social Information System) is partially digital but lacks AI means-testing. e-Otinish at KG scale ($5-8M) would dramatically improve targeting and reduce fraud. KG social protection fund reform is an active World Bank project component.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz multilingual interface. Income data cross-check adapted to UZ/KG available databases (less comprehensive than KZ). Cash payment fallback for rural unbanked recipients. Medical certification integration for disability benefits.

World Bank Kazakhstan Social Protection

global_cases.case_name: Japan Digital Agency — Post-COVID Government Digitalisation Sprint
global_cases.problem_solved: Japan's COVID response exposed the consequences of digital neglect: relief payments took 3+ months to reach citizens due to paper-based procedures, fax machines still used between ministries, and My Number (national ID) had 35% enrollment with zero digital utility. Digital Agency was created as a whole-of-government digital transformation unit reporting directly to Cabinet.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Japan Digital Agency (JDA): Cabinet-level agency with authority over IT standards across all ministries. My Number + My Number Card (physical + digital wallet on iPhone/Android) integration with health insurance, bank accounts, tax, and driver's licence. Digital Common Platform: API-first government system standards (no more legacy custom procurement — all systems must use standard APIs). Government cloud: Government System Standardisation Programme moving 1,700 government systems to cloud by 2025. AI: government-wide LLM policy (civils servants allowed Bing AI/Copilot with government tenant isolation).
global_cases.outcome_metrics: My Number digital card: 74M issued (60% of population). 1,200 government systems moved to cloud by 2025. Fax machine use: eliminated in 98% of government offices by 2024. COVID digital payments (2022 follow-up): 4 weeks vs 3 months for paper (2020). Government API standardisation: 300+ common APIs defined. JDA won Nikkei Digital Governance Award 2024.
global_cases.failure_modes: Old-guard resistance: METI and some LDP politicians publicly resisted My Number expansion (privacy concerns). Data breach: MHLW data leak from My Number linkage in 2023 (7.3M records) — required emergency security audit. Speed vs quality: rapid cloud migration created system incompatibilities requiring $400M rework.
global_cases.replicability_factors: JDA published methodology and lessons. KOICA references JDA for Korean-Japanese parallel approach. The COVID-disaster-driven urgency model (mandate digital before next crisis) is directly applicable to UZ/KG as both face natural disaster digital gaps.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Japan's Digital Agency model — Cabinet-level authority over IT standards, cloud mandate, API standardisation — is the governance model UZ MoDT should study. UZ currently lacks the cross-government authority to enforce API standards. The LESSON not the technology: create a Cabinet-level digital authority with real power to mandate standards. Budget: governance change, not technology spend.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Japan's model is too large and too expensive for direct KG replication. Key lesson: the UDP digital department (post-April 2026 reorganisation) IS the equivalent of JDA — Presidential Administration-level authority over digital standards. KG should formalize UDP's authority explicitly in the new Положение (regulation) being drafted.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Budget adaptation (Japan $2.8B → UZ $30-50M phased). API standards mandate via Presidential decree. Cloud migration starting with new systems only (legacy migration is too expensive in near term). Governance structure: Cabinet authority for digital standards enforcement.

Japan Ministry of Internal Affairs — Digital

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan AI for Critical Minerals Exploration (Kazakhmys/Altyntau)
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan holds 25% of world's chromite, 30% of manganese, and significant copper/gold deposits. Manual geological survey data interpretation required PhD geophysicists taking 6-18 months per prospect. AI-assisted mineral potential mapping using satellite imagery, historical geological survey data, and geophysical readings could reduce exploration cycle from 5 years to 18 months.
global_cases.architecture_summary: KazGeology AI platform (MIID — Ministry of Industry and Infrastructural Development): satellite multispectral analysis (Sentinel-2 + ASTER thermal) for surface mineralogy mapping; historical Soviet geological survey data digitisation (30,000+ reports scanned via OCR + NLP extraction); machine learning mineral potential model (random forest on geochemical + geophysical + remote sensing features). Commercial application: Kazakhmys Corporation using platform to prioritise 50+ exploration blocks. KazGeology also provides academic access to model outputs for 7 Central Asian universities.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Mineral prospect screening time: 12-week AI assessment vs 2-year traditional survey. 15 new exploration blocks identified with >80% confidence in 3 years. Cost per prospect assessment: 85% reduction. Soviet geological data digitised: 30,000+ documents now machine-readable. Kazakhmys confirmed 3 new copper deposits via AI-prioritised drilling.
global_cases.failure_modes: Soviet-era geological data quality inconsistency (different standards across decades). Model accuracy drops for deposit types not well-represented in training data. Legal rights to Soviet-era geological data unclear — some data legally contested. Validation drilling cost ($2-5M per prospect) still required to confirm AI predictions.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Free satellite data (Sentinel-2, ASTER). Kazakhstan's Soviet geological archive digitisation methodology applicable to UZ/KG who have similar archives. KazGeology has bilateral data-sharing protocols with CA neighbours. Critical minerals AI exploration is global trend with major donor interest (US DFC, EBRD).
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has gold, uranium, copper, molybdenum, and rare earth deposits with significant unexplored potential. Soviet geological archive at GIGEOS (State Institute of Geology) has same structure as Kazakhstan's. AI mineral exploration using free satellite data + digitised Soviet archives is achievable for $3-6M. US DFC (critical minerals financing), EBRD, and ADB are active funders in UZ mining sector.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has gold (Kumtor and 50+ unexplored deposits), antimony, and rare earths. Soviet geological archive in KG Geological Survey. AI mineral exploration is HIGH PRIORITY under KG's economic strategy. US DFC has specific critical minerals programme for KG. Budget: $3-5M. This is a convergent case: mining + digital + export revenue potential.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian-language Soviet archive OCR (similar quality issues as KZ). Adaptation of mineral potential model for KG's metamorphic geology (different from KZ's sedimentary basins). Legal framework for AI-generated prospect data as exploration licence basis. Environmental monitoring integration (avoid AI recommendations in protected areas).

sources.title: KazGeology — Official
Kazakhstan MIID Mining Sector
